543232|2026-06.headline: CAMS Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 18% YoY to a record INR183 crore, with margin up 270bps to 46.4% despite muted MF AUM growth.
543232|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 11.5% YoY to INR395 crore and EBITDA grew over 18% to INR183 crore, the highest ever, with PAT up 17%. MF revenue grew under 10% while non-MF revenue grew over 28%, led by Pay (up ~67-70%) and AIF (up ~25%), while KRA declined after the April 2026 pricing reset. Management said July AUM recovered strongly and expects FY27 blended revenue growth of about 13% and EBITDA growth of about 16%. Non-MF margin fell to about 13% in Q1 from over 17% last quarter, which management attributed mainly to the KRA dip.

financial_highlights.change: just under +15% YoY; market share about 67.2%

segments.name: Mutual fund (asset-based)
segments.commentary: MF revenue grew about 11% on asset-based revenue, with absolute MF revenue up under 10%; management sees no quarter-on-quarter yield decline. Equity AUM grew 17.6% and equity net sales and live SIP counts grew ahead of industry.

segments.name: Pay (payments)
segments.commentary: Grew just short of 70% YoY, driven mainly by credit card transactions after the PA licence; management said cards will be grown step by step given low margins.

segments.name: AIF / Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM crossed INR3.2 lakh crore, grew mid-20s (about 25%), with 50 new mandates won in the quarter.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); management expects recovery from Q2.

segments.name: SIF and GIFT City
segments.commentary: SIF: 11 unique SIFs launched, about INR12,000 crore accumulated and about INR1,000 crore net sales per month, nearly 50,000 investors. GIFT City retail: about INR750 crore AUM from first 10,000 investors.

segments.name: CAMS Repository, AA, pension
segments.commentary: Not yet EBITDA positive; management expects CAMSRep to turn EBITDA positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is near breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 blended non-MF revenue growth of about 20%, possibly 22-23%; MF revenue growth of at least 12%; blended revenue growth about 13% and EBITDA growth about 16%.
Non-MF margin expected to recover to about 17% for the year, 'close to 20%' by year-end, per management's varying comments.
Employee cost growth target about 5% YoY for FY27; total cost growth target below 10% per year for the next two to three years.
Enterprise headcount to fall about 5% in FY27; net employee cost benefit expected to be about 3-3.5% rather than 5%.
Operating margin expansion of about 1% a year, with possibility of 1.5%.
PAT margin expected to stay at about 30-31%; FY27 PAT growth about 31% if EBITDA growth is about 45%, per Ram Charan's answer.

On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, declining later; re-architecture total cost about INR500 crore, of which about INR290 crore capex, with about INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least another INR80 crore in the rest of FY27.
Depreciation expected to rise, not fall, for the rest of FY27 by INR4-5 crore, due to re-architecture capitalisation.
capex_capacity: On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, falling in later years as cloud migration progresses.
Re-architecture project cost about INR500 crore, of which INR123 crore spent so far; about INR290 crore to be capex on a 10-year amortisation.
About INR40 crore re-architecture capitalised in Q1 FY27; at least INR80 crore more expected in the rest of FY27.
Transaction acceptance module of new platform going live Aug-Sep; full transaction acceptance concept by year-end. Four of eight transaction types live; all expected by November.
About 10% of gross payload converted to AI-based acceptance at maker level, to scale to 100% in 12 months.
demand_pricing: Market conditions muted in April-June; July materially better, AUM close to INR60 lakh crore but not yet there.
SIP collections held at just under INR60,000 crore in Q1; SIP collections and unique investor base grew faster than industry.

Yields: no quarter-on-quarter decline in Q1; compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is now in the base; residual compression for the next 3-4 quarters expected to be small. Historical 2.5-3% annual yield decline cited as likely.
KRA: pricing reset from 1 April 2026 cut rates about 29-30%; some fetch services that were free are now priced. Management says pricing is uniform across KRAs.
Mid-size AMC renewals: a couple concluded and two in discussion; impact on pricing expected to be very muted and already in Q1 pricing.
Non-asset MF revenue down YoY on lower NFO activity, the NSE arrangement winding down and application fees; QoQ also hit by MF Central and OPE.

qa_highlights.question: Expected AUM growth and yield compression behind the 13% blended revenue guidance, and downside risk (line dropped, not answered in full)
qa_highlights.answer: Question was cut off by a line drop before management responded; the outlook was not restated in that exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How many mid-size AMCs are up for renewal this year and is their pricing impact already in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of mid-size AMC renewals concluded and two more are in discussion; the impact is expected to be very muted and is already in Q1 pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did KRA revenue fall when CDSL saw a much smaller hit from the same pricing reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Some fetch services that were free are now priced, applying equally to CAMS; the revenue mix differs (CAMS is about 70-75% MF, 25-30% non-MF including DP and broking). Management says pricing is uniform across KRAs and the Q1 impact was not large.

qa_highlights.question: Non-MF margin in Q1 and expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-MF margin was about 13% in Q1 versus about 17% plus last quarter, seen as a one-quarter KRA effect. Management expects about 17% for the year, and at least close to 20% by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How does SIF economics work for CAMS?
qa_highlights.answer: SIF schemes are priced at the same rates as equivalent MF schemes; set-up costs for the separate segregated schema (11 SIFs) are already in the base, and scale-up defrays them.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount reduction and employee cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise headcount is targeted to fall about 5% in FY27, with 2-3% already down; net employee cost benefit is expected at about 3-3.5% because AI and automation hires offset some exits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5% employee cost growth target medium-term, and what about margin expansion beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5% employee cost growth is an end-of-FY27 year-on-year target (about INR500 crore base, adding INR25-30 crore). Total cost growth is targeted below 10% a year for the next two to three years; margin expansion of about 1% a year, with a possibility of 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-asset MF revenue decline YoY despite transaction growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Most transactions are digital; only a subset of paper transactions is billed. The YoY drop was driven by lower NFO activity, the NSE arrangement winding down and application fees. QoQ was hit by MF Central and OPE.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are AI and automation gains, and what is the payments and yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits from the new platform are incremental, with productivity gains over about 3-4 years; cloud and hardware cost inflation will offset some. Payments growth is mainly credit cards under the PA licence and will be scaled step by step; nothing one-time. Yield compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is in the base; residual compression over 3-4 quarters is expected to be small, with a historical 2.5-3% annual decline.

qa_highlights.question: Capex, capitalisation and depreciation outlook, and implied PAT growth?
qa_highlights.answer: On-prem capex about INR75 crore; re-architecture cost about INR500 crore, INR290 crore capex, with INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least INR80 crore more in FY27. Depreciation to rise by INR4-5 crore for the rest of FY27. With EBITDA growth about 45%, PAT growth is about 31%; PAT margin expected at 30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: Non-MF EBITDA breakeven status by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Account aggregator, pension and CAMS Repository are not yet EBITDA positive; CAMSRep is expected to turn positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is almost at breakeven. Account aggregator adoption faces a bottleneck, mainly on the fintech and lending side.

risks_watch: Recovery in KRA revenue from Q2 FY27 after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); Q1 non-MF margin fell to about 13%, and management needs it near 17-20% by year-end.
MF AUM reached about INR56 lakh crore but has not yet hit close to INR60 lakh crore; April-June was muted and July recovery must hold.
Employee cost growth target of about 5% and total cost growth below 10% a year for two to three years; cloud and hardware cost inflation could offset AI-driven savings.
Re-architecture: about INR80 crore more capitalisation in FY27, rising depreciation, and transaction acceptance modules going live Aug-Sep with all eight transaction types live by November.
Yield: residual compression for 3-4 quarters expected to be small, with a historical 2.5-3% annual decline; mid-size AMC renewals in discussion (two pending).
Payments growth is concentrated in low-margin credit cards, so margin dilution is a risk if the mix shifts further toward cards.
Management's comments on non-MF margin varied (about 17% versus close to 20%), and the 1% vs 1.5% margin expansion remains unconfirmed.
key_quotes: So on a blended basis, 11.2% MF revenue growth, 28% plus non -MF growth.
And there was nothing onetime. We've said this in the past, Abhijeet, that to build the book, we never take anything onetime and then drop it in the next quarter.
We are not doing it today because there's a risk in kind of just blindly doing it.
So, you should look at our headcount currently to be just shy of 8,300 for the company.
543232|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth levers (Pay, AIF, SIF, GIFT City, new AMC logos) and on cost discipline, but cautious and hedged on KRA recovery, yield outlook and margin targets, with several answers saying "let's watch it" or "we'll see by year-end". Management was defensive about the KRA pricing comparison with CDSL and declined to give revenue numbers for ConsentPro.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, ~1% a year with possibility of 1.5%
rows.why: Operating EBITDA margin rose 270bps YoY to 46.4% in Q1 and management guides about 1% annual expansion (possibly 1.5%), backed by total cost growth under 10% and employee cost growth around 5%, though non-MF margin fell to about 13% from 17%+ and needs to recover to about 17% for FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No productive capacity expansion discussed; the only build is about INR75 crore of on-prem IT capex (tools, servers, storage, premises) plus the INR290 crore re-architecture capex (INR40 crore capitalised in Q1, at least INR80 crore more in FY27), which is platform spend rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Equity AUM grew 17.6%, MF AUM about INR56 lakh crore (just under +15% YoY) with July AUM close to INR60 lakh crore, SIP collections held near INR60,000 crore, and 50 new AIF mandates; but April-June was muted and MF revenue grew under 10%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at about INR75 crore on-prem plus the already-committed re-architecture spend of about INR500 crore total, with no new plant or capacity expansion signalled and utilisation not a relevant metric for this asset-light model.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said a 22-23% non-MF growth outcome is possible ('if you're lucky') against 20%+ guided, and a 1.5% margin expansion is 'yes' possible against 1%, but FY27 blended growth of 13% revenue and 16% EBITDA was only held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Non-MF margin guide was cut from close to 20% to about 17%, KRA rates fell about 29-30% with recovery only from Q2, and MF AUM at INR56 lakh crore has not reached the INR60 lakh crore level management needs; a yield decline of 2.5-3% a year is historically typical.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Transaction acceptance module of the new platform goes live Aug-Sep 2026, with four of eight transaction types live and all expected by November, and 11 SIFs already launched with about INR12,000 crore accumulated.

rows.label: KRA recovery from Q2 FY27 after April 2026 pricing reset
rows.why: KRA rates were cut about 29-30% from 1 April 2026 and revenue fell YoY, with management expecting recovery from Q2, but this is not yet visible in numbers and the reset was defended against the CDSL comparison.

rows.label: CAMSRep turns EBITDA positive on Q4 basis
rows.why: Management expects CAMS Repository to turn EBITDA positive on a Q4 basis, while Think Analytics is near breakeven and account aggregator is held back by a fintech/lending bottleneck.

rows.label: Mid-size AMC renewals and new AMC logos
rows.why: Two mid-size AMC renewals concluded and two more in discussion with pricing impact expected to be very muted and already in Q1; new logos are cited as a growth lever without a number.

tone.note: Management was confident on Pay, AIF (50 new mandates), SIF, GIFT City and cost discipline, but hedged on KRA recovery, yield outlook and the non-MF margin (cut from close to 20% to about 17%); analysts pressed on the KRA pricing gap versus CDSL, and one question on yield and downside risk was cut o

543232|2026-09.headline: CAMS Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 10% YoY to INR415 crore, with EBITDA up 13.5% to INR191 crore and margin at 46%.
543232|2026-09.overview: Operating revenue crossed INR400 crore for the first time, up 10% YoY, while EBITDA grew 13.5% to about INR191 crore after absorbing deferred employee increments from Q1. EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 46% and PAT rose 14.5% YoY. MF AUM grew about 12.5% to INR58.5 lakh crore (67% share), with equity AUM up 15.5% versus industry 15.2%. Non-MF revenue grew about 21-22% YoY to just under 16% of revenue, led by CAMSPay (up over 50% YoY) and KRA's recovery.

financial_highlights.change: +150 bps YoY; +11% QoQ growth in non-MF revenue
After ~INR160 crore dividends paid in quarter
Includes INR8.5 crore annual appraisal impact (~2%)

segments.name: Mutual fund (asset-based)
segments.commentary: CAMS MF AUM about INR58.5 lakh crore, up ~12.5%, 67% market share; equity AUM up 15.5% vs industry 15.2%, with ~70% share of industry equity net sales over last year. Gross SIP collections up 16.5% vs industry 12.4%.

segments.name: CAMSPay (payments)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 50% YoY and 13% QoQ; now over 6% of revenue (vs ~3% two to two-and-a-half years ago). Base now about INR100 crore-plus; management guides ~30% growth p.a. for next two years.

segments.name: KRA (KYC registration)
segments.commentary: Revenue rebounded QoQ despite price cut from April; share of demat/broking segment rising; 5 of top 10 broking houses are clients. Incremental revenue from Phase 1 status-inquiry APIs estimated at ~INR1.5 crore.

segments.name: Alternatives / AIF
segments.commentary: Revenue up 22% YoY; AUM just crossed INR3.3 lakh crore; 50-plus new mandates and 15 new marquee relationships. Management describes AIF as services-heavy with ~20% margin.

segments.name: Repository (demat and insurance)
segments.commentary: Crossed 15 million (1.5 crore) demat accounts; Bima Central broker module launched. Account aggregator revenue up 19% on a small base.

guidance_outlook: Yield: FY27 decline guided at ~3% YoY (less than 2.5% in a good quarter, ~3% in a reasonable quarter); QoQ decline was under 1%. Management sees no revision needed.
Non-MF: target ~20% growth and ~20% profitability exit; target non-MF share of sales to reach 20% within a couple of years. Non-MF margin steady-state of 25%+ seen in 3 years.

Expenses: management aims to keep expense growth below 10%; Q3 and Q4 platform costs expected to rise from ~INR5 crore to ~INR8 crore then ~INR9.5-10 crore per quarter, net incremental opex only ~INR1.5-2 crore per quarter after offsets.
CAMSPay growth: expect around early 30% per year over next two years rather than 50%.
Margins: normal years expected to expand 100-200 bps; new platform headcount trend (~250-300 fewer) expected to continue for at least 3 more years.
UPI MDR: limited upside, ~INR1-2 crore per year on a ~INR100 crore payments base.
Large AMC renewals: management says yield discounts will not be disproportionate; next year's renewals with a couple of large customers flagged.
capex_capacity: Re-architecture (FUNDSNet) platform about 30% complete; FUNDSNet live and legacy utility to be sunset by March/April 2027.
Cumulative platform cost taken to opex about INR27 crore to date; Q2 platform cost ~INR5 crore (INR2.5 crore opex plus INR1.5 crore depreciation, per CFO).
Depreciation rose INR3.5 crore QoQ to ~INR28 crore; more than INR1.5 crore attributed to new modules going live; storage server capitalisation also raised it.
Headcount about 8,200, down from ~8,450 at start of year (250-300 reduction through non-backfilling).
Several hundred crore of SEBI-mandated investment cited as a cost driver in yield negotiations.
GIFT City retail funds: AUM above INR1,500 crore after 5 launches, with 2-3 more expected in Q3. SIF AUM about INR20,000 crore across ~12 AMCs.
demand_pricing: Equity net sales share ~70% of industry over last year; gross SIP collections +16.5% YoY vs industry 12.4%.

Yield drop ~3% YoY attributed to scale-based telescopic pricing (~2% in a normal year), mix shift from debt to passives (debt yield ~2-2.25 bps replaced by passives ~0.5 bps), and customer mix; management denies large discounts or renewal discounts.
Client base: 32 of 64 licensed AMCs; InCred AMC appointed CAMS as RTA; ASK Investments and Carnelian went live; Oaklane and Neo expected in Q3.
Non-MF asset-linked vs transaction revenue: non-asset-based MF revenue (transactions, MFCentral, call centre, NFO) is not asset-linked; NFOs fell sharply YoY.
Competition: management says the industry faces pressure from AI-enabled in-sourcing and AMC price negotiations, but argues outsourcing persists at scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will CAMSPay growth moderate given the high base, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects around early 30% growth per year over the next two years rather than 50%, with 50% possibly lasting one or two more quarters; growth driven by cards business added on top of payment aggregator licence.

qa_highlights.question: How much of KRA's rebound is volume versus repricing, and is ~INR100 crore a quarter a fair run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to usage growth and new clients in demat/broking, with the Phase 1 API contributing only about INR1.5 crore incremental revenue; expects growth to continue over time, with no run-rate figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 employee cost a fair run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Q2 employee cost can be taken as run-rate, with no one-offs in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Could new AMCs or large-AMC renegotiations drag yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Newer AMCs (last 5 years) are estimated at 5-7% of AUM and revenue; management says better pricing on those young AMCs offsets; renewal discussions for large customers in FY28 will not be commented on yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new platform's P&L drag and trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Platform costs to rise from ~INR5 crore to ~INR8 crore, then ~INR9.5-10 crore per quarter over the next two quarters, but net incremental drag only ~INR1.5-2 crore per quarter after productivity offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Will UPI MDR benefit CAMSPay materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Very little: MDR of ~40 bps on UPI financial transactions versus ~2 bps on MF transactions, implying only ~INR1-2 crore a year benefit on a ~INR100 crore book.

risks_watch: Yield pressure: FY27 guided ~3% decline; renewal of a couple of large AMC contracts in FY28 is an open question and management declined to comment on terms.
AI and digital disruption of RTA/outsourcing models; management says in-sourcing is still distant but flagged possible digital regulation impact in next 2-3 quarters.
Platform cost ramp: Q3 and Q4 platform costs expected to rise to INR8-10 crore per quarter before offset by productivity; headcount reduction must sustain.
AUM growth moderation: management acknowledges that MF AUM growth of 7-8% would require a different response; cost control depends on productivity.
CAMSPay growth normalising from 50% toward ~30%; KRA revenue sensitive to capital market activity.
543232|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on earnings quality and cost control, with emphasis that Q2 was not one-off; cautious and evasive on FY28 large-AMC renewals and on the AI/digital disruption question, which management answered only in general terms.
key_quotes: This is the first time we have crossed the INR400 crores mark.
The good news is that this is not a cash-guzzling business.
We will continue to remain a sold product, a significantly sold product, not a sought product.
So overall, this business, the non-MF business, grew almost 22%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 100-200 bps margin expansion in normal years and EBITDA margin already rose 140 bps YoY to 46%, but Q3-Q4 platform costs rise to ~INR9.5-10 crore per quarter, with net drag of only ~INR1.5-2 crore per quarter after offsets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; the only build is the FUNDSNet software re-architecture (~30% complete, sunset by March/April 2027), which is a platform, not physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: MF AUM up ~12.5% to INR58.5 lakh crore, equity AUM +15.5% vs industry 15.2%, gross SIP collections +16.5% vs industry 12.4%, and CAMSPay guided at ~30% growth p.a. for two years, though yield falls ~3% in FY27 and AUM growth of 7-8% would need a different response.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Depreciation rose to ~INR28 crore and the platform is being built internally; no utilisation level was given and no new capex programme was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance (yield decline ~3%, expense growth below 10%, non-MF ~20% growth) and sees no revision needed, with no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Yield drop of ~3% in FY27 with a large AMC renewal open for FY28, digital regulation flagged for the next 2-3 quarters, and CAMSPay normalising from 50% toward ~30%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Oaklane and Neo onboarding expected in Q3, 2-3 more GIFT City retail fund launches expected in Q3, and CAMSPay card business is scaling on top of the payment aggregator licence.

rows.label: Non-MF revenue scaling toward 20% of sales
rows.why: Non-MF revenue grew ~21-22% YoY to just under 16% of revenue, with non-MF profitability near 19% vs under 15% last quarter and a ~20% FY27 exit target.

rows.label: AIF and GIFT City expansion
rows.why: AIF AUM crossed INR3.3 lakh crore with 50-plus new mandates and 15 new marquee relationships, and GIFT City retail AUM is above INR1,500 crore with 2-3 more launches in Q3.

rows.label: Headcount reduction via non-backfilling
rows.why: Headcount fell from ~8,450 to ~8,200 (250-300 fewer) and management expects the trend to continue for at least 3 more years.

tone.note: Management was confident on earnings quality, cost control and the ~3% yield guide, and cautious or evasive on FY28 large-AMC renewals and AI/digital disruption; analysts pressed on CAMSPay normalisation, yield pressure and the platform cost ramp.

543235|2026-03.headline: Angel One Q4 FY26: gross income up 9.7% QoQ to ₹14.7 bn, net income up 10.4% to ₹11.3 bn, reported EBDAT margin 41.7%.
543235|2026-03.overview: Orders executed rose 13.3% QoQ to 431 mn despite one fewer trading day, with broking at 60.7% of gross income. Reported EBDAT margin expanded 227 bps QoQ to 41.7%, and normalized margin (ex one-time items and IPL) rose 498 bps to 44.4%. PAT grew 19.2% QoQ to ₹3.2 bn. Management flagged softer distribution revenue (credit and IPO related) and a one-time ₹192 mn client goodwill reimbursement, and proposed capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 bn each into the wealth and NBFC businesses.

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized EBDAT margin (ex one-time and IPL)

segments.name: Broking (Direct + Assisted)
segments.commentary: Commodity broking income up 15.8% QoQ, F&O revenue up 16.1% QoQ, cash segment up 4.6% QoQ. Assisted (AP) channel is about 25-27% of broking revenue; direct about 75%.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue moderated QoQ due to lower credit distribution and softer IPO activity, partly offset by insurance distribution growth. Management called these trends cyclical.

segments.name: Wealth (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed ₹100 bn, up 23% QoQ; UHNI business grew 2x over 12 months; AUM per RM up 3x YoY; over 45% of 1,900+ clients from non-metros. Breakeven guided in about 3-3.5 years.

segments.name: Asset Management (AMC)
segments.commentary: Period-end AUM ₹3.6 bn, down sequentially on softer markets and liquid fund redemptions; folios up 28% QoQ to over 246,000; scheme count 11 after Silver ETF launches.

segments.name: Credit
segments.commentary: Lifetime cumulative disbursements ₹27.1 bn, with ₹6.1 bn disbursed in Q4. Distribution only, no FLDG or credit risk on the books; loan-against-securities to be launched via NBFC on own balance sheet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 employee cost including ESOP expected flat with FY26 (about ₹11 bn); ESOP numbers to be finalized, detail promised for July call.
Operating margin drag from newer businesses for FY26 guided at about 2.5-3%.
Management expects further margin expansion in broking and distribution; cited FY28 margins above 45% but declined to give a specific exit-rate number.
Second half FY26 margin (around 42-43%) to be the base for FY27, per management.
IPL spend for the full season about ₹1.5 bn, with a lower amount booked in Q4 because the season started late in March.
Tax rate expected to move to about 25-26% of PBT as newer businesses scale and deductions reduce.
Cost of acquisition expected to stay in a similar range; no client addition target given.
capex_capacity: Proposed capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 bn each into the wealth management business and the NBFC platform.
Loan-against-securities product to be launched on NBFC balance sheet with pledged AUM as credit limit.
Temporary liquidity arrangements used around the 1 April 2026 banking holiday contributed to elevated borrowings.
Ask Angel AI assistant embedded across app journeys; more than 50% of development augmented by AI; 80% of Ionic Wealth code base AI-generated.
demand_pricing: Average daily orders rose from 5 mn in Feb 2025 to 7.4 mn in Mar 2026; Q4 aggregate 431 mn orders, a six-quarter high.
Retail equity turnover share 20.4%, up 46 bps YoY; demat market share 16.7%, up 54 bps YoY.

Equity market share (cash plus F&O premium) up 46 bps YoY but down 4 bps QoQ; cash share down 117 bps QoQ and 37 bps YoY; F&O premium share up 51 bps QoQ and 77 bps YoY; commodity share up 100 bps QoQ but down YoY.
Cash segment realization fell in Q4; management attributed this to March client mix and sharp market fall, without quantifying.
Management said March saw fewer users returning, with higher-value clients staying active while low-end users exited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NSE active client count flat despite higher order run rates, and how should customer acquisition costs and cost optimization evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSE active is a 12-month metric and the industry has started adding net clients again; CAC guided as stable and not disclosed separately. Monthly client acquisitions are disclosed monthly.

qa_highlights.question: What was the ₹192 mn one-time item and is there recourse?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhavin Parekh said a technical issue at the MII level caused an abnormal trading environment; the company paid a goodwill gesture with no obligation. It is working with the MII to recover the amount.

qa_highlights.question: Why did market share in cash fall, and what about commodity yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March drove the cash share dip due to client mix and market fall, with an expected April rebound. Commodity growth was attributed to market expansion, with no structural mix shift seen.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit volume drop seasonal, and is there any FLDG or credit risk on the books?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh Agarwal said the dip is not seasonal, with ecosystem challenges in Q4. No FLDG and no credit risk on the books in the distribution business.

qa_highlights.question: What operating margin drag and breakeven timeline apply to new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Drag guided at about 2.5-3% for FY26. Wealth breakeven is 3-3.5 years away; management said newer businesses should be evaluated separately from broking.

qa_highlights.question: How does the MTF book behave and what is the outlook?

543235|2026-06.headline: Angel One Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25.4% YoY to ₹14.3 billion and PAT rose 102.1% YoY to ₹2.3 billion, while sequential revenue slipped 2.3%.

Reported EBDAT was ₹3.6 billion (32.7% margin), and management said normalized EBDAT margin was 43.6% versus 44.4% last quarter after adjusting for IPL spend, increments, variable pay and fresh ESOP grants. Interest income rose 2.6% QoQ to ₹4.7 billion, with the period-end client funding book at a record ₹71.5 billion. Credit distribution grew 130% YoY to ₹5.3 billion, but management did not explain the quarter-on-quarter softness in disbursals that analysts raised.

segments.name: Client funding (MTF)
segments.commentary: Interest income ₹4.7 billion, 32.6% of gross revenue. Average book ₹61.4 billion and period-end book ₹71.5 billion; 83% of exposure is below ₹100,000 per client.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 3% of revenue and moderated QoQ on seasonally weaker insurance sales and muted credit disbursement. Lending is run through 7 lending partners.

segments.name: Wealth management (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: Wealth-tech AUM crossed ₹32.3 billion; UHNI AUM ₹87.3 billion across 263 families; total wealth AUM ₹134.4 billion (+33.3%). Revenue not disclosed; burn about 4% of consolidated operating margin for AMC and wealth combined this quarter.

segments.name: Asset management (AMC)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed ₹6.2 billion. Currently passive-only; product rollout mostly happened in the last quarter of FY26, and management said it is evaluating an expanded product suite.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a 45% to 50% margin guidance on an adjusted basis, with the 40% to 45% standalone range referenced in analyst questions; it said the guidance is intact.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit disbursement declined over recent quarters (about ₹710 crore at Q3, ₹610 crore, then ₹530 crore), and what has not worked?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh Agarwal cited customer sentiment, lender underwriting and pricing, and platform friction as causes. Management said lenders are recalibrating risk and pricing, and that some funnel friction is being fixed. It maintained that the long-term thesis is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How is broking trending in July after a weak start, and how should the next quarters look?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said only about 15 days of July were available, so there is too early a read. He said nothing fundamental had changed and that the company does not comment on mid-quarter volumes or MTF run rates.

qa_highlights.question: Wealth management revenue, cost and breakeven plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Agrawal said wealth and AMC revenue are not disclosed. Burn is about 4% of operating margin this quarter, expected at 3% to 3.5% for FY27, with incremental breakeven in about 3 to 4 years. No absolute quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AMC's AUM still small after launch, and what is the plan?

qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said risk is limited because margins follow exchange-prescribed levels and sometimes exceed them. Vineet Agrawal added that the company has seen no issues in past market shocks and sees low penetration among its clients.

543235|2026-09.headline: Angel One Q2 FY27: consolidated PAT up 58.2% YoY to ₹3.35 bn on revenue of ₹14.3 bn (+18.9%); standalone OPM 48.9%.

Consolidated operating margin rose to 45.1% from 34.5% a year ago; normalised for IPL spend and ESOP reversals it was 43.8% versus 43.6% in Q1. Management kept the standalone broking-plus-distribution margin guidance at about 45% annually and reported record average funding book (₹74.5 bn) and record credit distribution in September (annualised run rate ₹33 bn). Client additions were about 1.5 mn, up 11.6% QoQ. Management said October F&O industry ADTO was up about 39% month-to-date versus September (as of 14 October) and linked near-term upside to the SEBI closing auction session (CAS) circular.

543245|2026-06.headline: Gland Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR18,003 million, adjusted EBITDA margin 28%, PAT up 47% to INR3,170 million.

Adjusted EBITDA (after adding back ESOP) was INR5,102 million at 28% margin, up from 25%, while reported EBITDA was INR4,930 million after a INR36 million forex loss. PAT rose 47% YoY to INR3,170 million but fell versus Q4 FY26, which had a INR508 million forex gain. Management announced a 55-SKU, USD90-100 million potential CDMO supply deal, a China-sourced liposomal in-licence, and a INR2,000 crore capex programme now being executed; Saudi Arabia NUPCO tender delays hit rest-of-world sales.

qa_highlights.answer: Partner is a global specialty pharma company; about 30-40% of revenue is specialty. Products are made in Indian sites; split is about 60% U.S., 30-35% Europe, 15-20% ROW. Tech transfer starts September 2026, first products in 24 months, ramp from 2029 to 2030.

543248|2026-03.headline: RBA India Q4 FY26 SSSG hit 6.3%, the highest in 12 quarters, while Indonesia took a INR120 crore impairment and the company is being acquired by Inspira Global.
543248|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 SSSG of 6.3%, up from 4.5% in the prior quarter, with full-year SSSG at 4%. Full-year revenue was INR2,271 crore, restaurant EBITDA margin 11.6% and company EBITDA margin 5.8%. Gross margin exited Q4 at 70.2%, ahead of the FY29 target. Indonesia drew a INR120 crore impairment on a DCF valuation, with Popeyes (24 outlets) losing IDR25 billion, and the company is set to be acquired by Inspira Global, with revised outlook promised after the deal closes in Q1.

qa_highlights.answer: Sumit said cash is about INR190 crore as of March, cash from operations rose from INR99 crore to INR132 crore, and India is targeting FCF neutrality in 4-6 quarters. Q4 generated INR40 crore. Analyst confirmed FY28 FCF-positive target; management agreed.

qa_highlights.answer: Impairment came from a DCF on consolidated Indonesia business; management called it a one-time provision fully covering the balance-sheet requirement. 543252|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.2% YoY to Rs 117 crore, but EBITDA margin rose to 6.9% on better domestic realisations as Chinese dumping eased.
543252|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 117 crore, down 3.2% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 8 crore at a 6.9% margin and adjusted PAT of Rs 3.7 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to better domestic price realisation as Chinese dumping of dimer acid moderated from around February 2026. For FY26, revenue fell 14.5% to Rs 460 crore on volume of 44,000 tonnes versus 54,000 tonnes in FY25. Management guided to 75-80% capacity utilisation on the 80,000-tonne base in FY27 and targets around 8% EBIT margin, with a new 40,000-tonne oleochemical product line planned for commissioning in Q2 FY27.

543252|2026-06.headline: Fairchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34.4% YoY to Rs 176 crore and EBITDA margin reached 10.14%, driven by price realisation.
543252|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 176 crore, up 34.4% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 18 crore (10.14% margin) and net profit of Rs 10 crore. Management attributed the gain mainly to higher price realisation, linked to elevated raw material costs, lower imports amid Middle East supply disruption, and reduced Chinese dumping. Sales volume was 13,500 tonnes versus 13,000 tonnes in Q1 FY26, while utilisation is near 60% against a target exit of 70-75% for FY27. Isostearic acid remains small (4% of revenue) with slow customer qualification.

segments.name: Isostearic acid
segments.commentary: About 4% of Q1 revenue; sold into cosmetics, qualification slow as only three global manufacturers exist.

segments.commentary: Approximately 24% of Q1 revenue.

Capacity utilisation to rise by about 5% per quarter, to about 70-75% exit FY27 from roughly 60% now (on 80,000 tonne capacity).
A new oleochemical product is to start trial runs from Q2 FY27 on a 40,000 tonne capacity; ramp-up only after stabilisation; management says margins should be better than current.
Isostearic acid expected to exceed 80% capacity utilisation in 1-2 years; management indicated a positive outcome by end FY27 at some customers.
Export share currently 7-8% of revenue; management expects export growth from dimer and Isostearic acid, aided by India-UK and India-EU FTAs and rupee depreciation.
Management is not planning debt-funded or aggressive expansion given business risk.

demand_pricing: Price realisation up ~30% vs Q1 FY26 and ~25% vs Q4 FY26; management says raw material cost increases were passed through due to Middle East supply constraints and lower imports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable if supply constraints ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company cannot control renewed dumping; it called sustainability uncertain and cited business risk as the reason for avoiding debt-funded expansion.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 50 lakh is spent on revenue R&D, with the CFO stating 1-1.5% of sales; the company will check the annual report disclosure.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals from cosmetics buyers in Europe and Japan are slow; the company is at step 3 or beyond everywhere and expects a possible positive outcome by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation change and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation up about 25% from Q4 FY26 and about 30% from Q1 FY26; management hopes it holds as long as the West Asia crisis continues.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is happy with realisations and aims to reach 100% utilisation before ramping capacity further, with market share gains as the focus.

543252|2026-09.headline: Fairchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 49.7% YoY to Rs 167 crore at a 10.5% EBITDA margin, helped by lower raw material costs after the crude soybean oil duty cut.
543252|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 167 crore (up 49.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 10.5% and net profit of Rs 10.2 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 343 crore (up 41.4%), EBITDA Rs 35.4 crore at a 10.3% margin, and net profit Rs 21.2 crore. Management attributed gains to better price realisation from lower raw material costs, higher finished product prices, and lower dimer acid imports. Plant utilisation is still low at about 60-65%, and management expects it to improve as raw material availability rises after the crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Raw material and import duty
segments.commentary: Crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%, versus earlier 27% duty on crude oils that management said made raw material too expensive. Management called the lower duty the new run rate, said some benefit is already in H1 via inventory, and said market prices are starting to soften. It declined to share the raw material mix.

segments.name: Capacity and utilisation
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 60-65% (CFO: close to 65%). Management targets 5% improvement every quarter but gave no timeline for reaching 85-90%. Management says it has not lost market share.

segments.name: New fatty-acid product
segments.commentary: Small-capacity plant using novel technology, import-substituting with export potential; commissioning has slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec quarter (after Diwali), with start-up hiccups expected. Management said the market is very large if the process succeeds, and a PFAD bypass product from palm oil is already commercialised and is a different product.

segments.name: Exports and pricing
segments.commentary: Realisation Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26. Exports to the US are on hold due to high freight costs. Value-added products (linoleic acid, distilled dimer) are expected to earn a 5-10% realisation premium. Chinese dumping has fallen, mainly due to lower Chinese export incentives, with rupee depreciation also helping.

segments.name: Isostearic Acid and cosmetics
segments.commentary: Cosmetics business is expected to be hit in the near term by slowing European demand and high US import duties. Approval cycle took 2.5 years. Management expects long-term recovery since only four players globally make the product, and sees UK as the sole Cargill plant location.

segments.name: Working capital and cash use
segments.commentary: Working capital cycle guided at 90-100 days for domestic sales, longer for exports, around 100 days overall; trade receivables about Rs 100 crore. No near-term expansion plans; capex only if the new product succeeds; land of Rs 12 crore bought from promoter, already in use for operations and workers' colony.

qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 versus Rs 130/kg in Q1 and Rs 106/kg a year ago. Management said it does not expect China to restart dumping, citing lower export incentives.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would like to see 15-18% and expects to maintain the current margin, trying to improve it further. It declined to share the raw material mix.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said European cosmetic demand is slowing and the approval cycle took 2.5 years. It expects long-term recovery because only four players make the product, and said there is no need for knee-jerk action.

543253|2026-03.headline: Mrs. Bectors FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore (+9.1%) but EBITDA grew only 2.5% to INR257.7 crore, with margin at 12.6%.
543253|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 8.9% YoY to INR485.86 crore, with Biscuits up 8.4% and Bakery up 8.5%, and Bakery EBITDA margin at 12.7% (+25 bps). FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,043.6 crore (+9.1%), EBITDA INR257.7 crore (+2.5%, margin 12.6%) and PAT INR140.9 crore (6.9% margin). Management flagged a new cost shock from the West Asia conflict (about 3% cost impact on packaging, palm oil, crude-linked items, labour and logistics), which it says is covered by price increases and Project IMPACT savings. Export incentive (DFIA) remains on hold, and exports stayed in low-single-digit growth in Q4.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.4% YoY and FY26 grew 6.7%; management targets low-to-mid-teens growth in FY27. About 65% of biscuit sales come from INR5 and INR10 packs.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, NaturBaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 8.5% with Navratri shifting into March. FY26 grew 14%. Management guides mid-teens Bakery growth in FY27, with English Oven at high-teens and QSR at low-teens. Premiumisation is about 55-56% for English Oven.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Low-single-digit growth in Q4 and single-digit for FY26, hit by US tariffs (peak 50%) and the West Asia conflict. FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens growth; the Bahrain and Kuwait GCC markets are affected.

segments.name: Frozen / value-added bakery
segments.commentary: Sells raw dough, baked bread and ready sandwiches, partly sourced from third parties. Growing month-on-month on quick commerce in Delhi NCR. NaturBaked targets about INR10 crore ARR.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Biscuits growth guided at low-to-mid-teens; Bakery at mid-teens; exports at low-to-mid-teens.

A Bangalore facility is under consideration. Each plant is planned to produce burger buns and value-added products, including sourdough and frozen dough.
demand_pricing: Competitor INR4.5 pack pricing post GST 2.0 hurt Q3 and Q4 biscuit volumes; management called it an aberration and said one large player is still transitioning to the right coin pricing.

US tariffs were cut from their 50% peak, and new US retailer projects have started onboarding. Export incentive (DFIA) restart is still pending with the government.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the current RM and wheat inflation, and can margins be protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil, crude-linked items and packaging are the main drivers. Total impact is about 3% including labour and logistics, mostly covered by pricing and cost efficiency, with logistics impact still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bakery growth slow to 9% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Navratri moved into March (from April last year), which hit bread demand in North India. Management called it seasonal and said English Oven is still growing at high-teens.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin hold YoY and can it reach 14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin improvement in Q1 and Q2, and says margin should be maintained YoY unless crude spikes sharply. It stated the objective is to get as close as possible to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook and status of the export incentive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew in single digits in FY26 and low single digits in Q4; FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens. The DFIA incentive restart is still pending, and cost and price actions partly offset its loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of INR5 and INR10 packs and is there commodity hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: INR5 and INR10 packs make up about 65% of biscuit sales, in line with the industry. Hedging is selective, and the hedge levels are not disclosed.

Khopoli bun line utilisation was not disclosed, and the new Mumbai plant is still ramping up.
Minimum wage hikes in UP and Karnataka add to cost pressure.

543254|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to ₹269 crore, but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹45 crore (16.8% margin) and PAT dropped to ₹0.7 crore after one-offs.
543254|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 6% YoY to ₹269 crore on higher volumes and tariff escalation. EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% a year ago, driven by higher transport/hiring costs at the CIDCO site, employee costs rising to 34% of revenue, and about ₹10 crore of deferred Q4 FY26 disposal work. The PCMC WtE plant was shut after a July 8 landslide of legacy waste that killed nine people, and management flagged a ₹22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) as an exceptional item. The company also refinanced ₹140 crore of Antony Lara's term loan from 10.25% to 8.25%, with a ₹7 crore prepayment charge.

rows.why: Andhra Pradesh WtE (Kadapa, Kurnool) is already under construction with financial closure near final, and Q1 borrowings rose ~₹22 crore QoQ, but no new capex plant was announced and utilisation was not disclosed; the C&T&D plant runs at ~100% of its 600 tpd capacity, which supports a future expansion announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Transport vendor renegotiation and labour-cost pass-through

543257|2026-03.headline: IRFC FY26 sanctions reached ~INR74,000 crore and disbursements ~INR35,000 crore, with Q4 PAT flat quarter-on-quarter at ~INR1,684 crore.
543257|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue and PAT (crossing INR7,000 crore) and net worth of INR56,000-odd crore, with AUM up to INR4.85 lakh crore on a net basis. Q4 PAT was flat as new RBI-linked provisioning on non-railway (CPSE and state-government) lending and higher CSR spend offset revenue growth of about 9%. The company is diversifying beyond Indian Railways, earning NIMs of 100-120 bps on new assets against about 35-40 bps on railway business. No numeric FY27 guidance was given; management set a benchmark of repeating FY26 sanction and disbursement volumes and targeted double-digit growth in top line, PAT, EPS and NIM.

segments.commentary: Margins fixed at ~35 bps for projects and ~40 bps for rolling stock; zero provisioning required on sovereign exposure. Repayments of ~INR20,000 crore per year expected from this book.

segments.name: Diversified / non-railway lending
segments.commentary: FY26 new business ~INR35,000 crore disbursed, about 5% of AUM, at 100-120 bps margins. Marquee deals: ~INR10,000 crore refinance of DFCCIL World Bank loan and >INR12,000 crore refinance of HURL (NTPC/IOCL/Coal India JV) in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; benchmark set at FY26 levels of ~INR75,000 crore sanctions and ~INR35,000 crore disbursements, with management expecting to surpass them.
AUM expected to cross INR5 lakh crore in H1 FY27, possibly earlier, and then be maintained.

Top line expected to grow more than 10% in FY27, visible from Q1.
Long-term target mix of roughly 60% railways and 40% non-railway, with 30-40% non-railway aspired near term.

demand_pricing: Competitive market: IRFC wins more than 60% of bids it participates in against NBFCs and banks; banks now offering 10-year tenors.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sanctions and disbursements, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sanctions were ~INR74,000 crore and disbursements ~INR35,000 crore; management expects FY27 sanctions above INR75,000 crore and disbursements again above INR35,000 crore, without firm numeric guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What spread is IRFC earning on new lending and what are competitors offering?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins on new business are 100-120 bps versus 35-40 bps on railway business; IRFC competes with NBFCs and banks on A to AAA assets and wins more than 60% of bids.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA on new versus legacy business, adjusted for tax and provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure. It said ROA was 1.39% (up from 1.34%), that the mix target is 60:40, and that tax is largely absent for 5-7 years because of accumulated depreciation. It declined to validate an analyst's ~2% estimate for new business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60:40 railway/non-railway mix realistic, and does it need ~INR1 lakh crore a year of disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ~INR20,000 crore of annual repayments from railways means the required base is smaller; it aspires to 30-40% non-railway in the near term and 40-60% over 3-5 years, not a fixed target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall and why did OCI drop by about INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new provisioning on CPSE and state-government lending, higher CSR spend and lower other income (a tax refund interest item in Q3). OCI reflects mark-to-market on hedged foreign-currency borrowings for non-railway lending, which is temporary under Ind AS 109 cash-flow hedge accounting.

qa_highlights.question: How will IRFC keep zero NPA as it lends to state governments and other entities?
qa_highlights.answer: It lends only to CPSE subsidiaries (NTPC, GAIL, Coal India, IOCL) and to GenCos and TransCos with PPA and cost-plus structures; it avoids DISCOMs and high-consumption southern states. Examples include MAHAGENCO, Chhattisgarh and Haryana.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding strategy and liquidity plan?
qa_highlights.answer: ECB target of 30-35% of the borrowing mix; the company has done yen ECBs of $300 million, $400 million, and has a $1.1 billion yen bid open. Bonds at 5.25% and a zero-coupon bond were issued; 54EC bonds are being targeted.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT was flat QoQ and, per the analyst, fell about INR100 crore; provisioning on non-railway exposure is a new drag to watch.
Rising interest rates and domestic bond costs may pressure margins; management said rates are being revised upward.
Competition for the NTPC/UP JV tender (INR28,000-29,000 crore) and other large RFPs could compress margins from the 100-120 bps target.

543257|2026-06.headline: IRFC Q1 FY27: disbursement slow at about INR2,000 crore and AUM dipped QoQ, but management reiterates about INR5 lakh crore year-end AUM.
543257|2026-06.overview: Management framed FY27 as a consolidation year, building toward 2030 midterm and 2037 long-term plans after FY26 agreements above INR75,000 crore and disbursements above INR35,000 crore. Q1 disbursement was about INR2,000 crore and AUM declined slightly on an accrual basis, which management attributed to scheduled repayments from railways that fall in September. Management said the company is now a near-record on revenue and PAT, helped by a forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements. The call focused on the "Fund in India" conduit model, high-speed rail and DFC pipeline, NIM targets, and questions on fertiliser exposure and the agreement-to-disbursement lag.

segments.name: Railways (core, sole financier)
segments.commentary: Management says IRFC remains the sole financing arm for Indian Railways; no railway business was booked in FY24 but FY26 saw a restart in diversification. Railway repayments drive quarterly AUM dips.

segments.name: Diversified / non-railway (fertiliser, metro, GenCo, ports)
segments.commentary: Three HURL urea plants (Gorakhpur, Barauni, Sindri) are financed on railway-linkage grounds, refinanced from SBI-led lenders at 50bps+ lower cost. Hyderabad Metro Phase 1 refinancing signed; Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) pending decision.

guidance_outlook: Year-end FY27 AUM targeted around INR5 lakh crore (management: possibly INR4.95 lakh crore); mid-year guidance of about INR5 lakh crore also referenced.
FY27 disbursement guided to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore; Q2-Q4 expected to pick up, with some refinancing assets in the pipeline.
NIM target: about 10bps average annual improvement, 2% by end-2030; FY27 NIM targeted above 1.6%, with Q4 NIM expected to be higher than the 1.65% full-year ambition referenced by the analyst.

Planning around INR50,000-plus crore disbursement per year for the next decade; high-speed rail and DFC pipeline cited as more than INR50,000-60,000 crore per year, with metro and rapid rail adding INR20,000-30,000 crore per year.
Targets new lending at about 8% with spread above 100bps; repayments on legacy assets at 35-40bps lower margin.
capex_capacity: Planned high-speed rail corridors (7 announced) with financing need about INR16 lakh crore; DFC about INR3 lakh crore; combined about INR20 lakh crore, per management.
Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore; Phase 1 refinancing already signed.
Greenfield projects take 3 to 5 years from agreement to first funding, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says recent open-tender rates for GenCo and transport projects are around 8%, and IRFC is comfortable lending at that level with 100bps+ margin.
Fund in India: IRFC intends to act as a conduit for bilateral and multilateral funding, offering bespoke tenor and currency solutions.
Competitors' NIMs are falling across the sector per management; IRFC's low overhead cost is cited as the advantage.
Q1 disbursement was small because the pipeline is thin; management says it is not reliant on FY26 agreements converting in-year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hold the INR5 lakh crore AUM guidance at half-year and end FY27, and what is the disbursement and AUM growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about INR5 lakh crore AUM by year-end, noting it may land at INR4.95 lakh crore. FY27 disbursement is expected to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore. The Q1 AUM dip reflects a September repayment from railways.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 2% YoY against AUM growth of about 4%, implying NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM rose from 1.40% in FY25 to 1.50% in FY26 and is expected to exceed 1.6% by year-end. Legacy 35-40bps assets are repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets, which is a gradual effect over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the material other income in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements, reflecting rupee appreciation against the yen. Management said the gain is accounted per Ind AS and a corresponding metro receipt is expected in Q2. Last year's Q4 saw a INR7 crore forex loss.

qa_highlights.question: How are the fertiliser borrowers linked to railways, and is there sponsor support or guarantee for these loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HURL urea plants depend on railway sidings for raw material and finished urea movement. Output is sold to government agencies on a cost-plus model with 10-12% margin. Management described the loans as refinancing of an existing SBI-led bank facility, with rate cuts of at least 50bps. No explicit sponsor guarantee was described.

qa_highlights.question: What does the agreements-executed versus disbursement table mean, and why is there a lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR92,799 crore of agreements were largely greenfield, of which about INR37,000 crore has been disbursed. Greenfield funding typically starts 3 to 5 years after agreement, with the remainder expected over 1 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on diversification into metro and infrastructure, and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hyderabad Metro is on track, with Phase 1 refinancing signed and Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) awaiting a decision. Pipeline spans high-speed rail, DFC, metro, rapid rail, ports, GenCo, transco and renewables linked to railways.

risks_watch: Q1 disbursement of about INR2,000 crore leaves the INR35,000 crore-plus FY27 target dependent on a steep ramp in Q2-Q4.
AUM guidance hinges on repayments from railways and new refinancing deals; a September repayment could again lower the AUM figure.
NIM guidance (1.6%+ this year, 2% by 2030) relies on legacy assets at 35-40bps repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets; the call did not provide a quarterly path.
Fertiliser exposure to sister-company-linked borrowers; management cited cost-plus economics but no formal guarantee was described.
Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 decision and the high-speed rail and DFC funding framework remain unconfirmed; the large INR20 lakh crore opportunity is not yet contracted.
Forex gains on yen funding may not recur; the Q1 other income is currency-driven.

543257|2026-09.headline: IRFC reports H1 FY27 revenue up over 20% and PAT up over 10%; management reiterates ~INR5 lakh crore AUM target for FY27.
543257|2026-09.overview: Management said H1 FY27 beat both company guidance and street expectations, with revenue up more than 20% and PAT up more than 10% year on year. The CEO said PAT grew in double digits in five of the last six quarters, the exception being Q4 FY26, which carried provisions for new business under RBI norms. Diversification beyond the Indian Railways single-client model is the core theme, with non-railway lending at margins 2-3.5 times the railway book. The call also covered a large pipeline of railway-linked financing (DFC, high-speed rail, freight JVs) that management expects to start in FY28. Most Q&A was on strategy and shareholder value; the transcript gives no reported Q2 figures beyond the H1 growth rates.

segments.name: Railways (IR) lending
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% plus of AUM is with Railways, at a NIM of about 1.3% (around 35 bps margin on cost-plus). Railway book is being replaced over time by higher-yield non-IR assets.

segments.name: Non-railway lending (diversification)
segments.commentary: Non-IR assets earn margins of 2-3.5 times the railway book, per management; INR35,000 crore of disbursement last year was non-IR. Pipeline covers metros, ports, renewables, thermal power, Gencos linked to Railways, and some road linkages, targeted for Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements to exceed last year's level; guidance reiterated.
AUM target of near INR5 lakh crore (possibly slightly short by INR1,000-2,000 crore) by end FY27; management expects to show progress by Q3.
PAT expected to grow near 10% annually even with flat AUM, as non-IR assets replace railway assets at higher yields.

Railway-related funding of minimum about INR50,000 crore a year from FY28 for next decade, subject to the funding model (multilateral/aggregator role) to be finalised by end FY27; clearer numbers promised in Q3.
Mix target of 60% pure railways and 40% diversification by 2030.
Margin floor of INR0.85-0.90 per the ALM policy on non-railway loans; WACC target of 6.55% to be maintained.
capex_capacity: Management cited a Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat (over 2,000 km, more than INR3 lakh crore), seven sanctioned high-speed rail corridors, and six freight lines planned under JV/PPP; total pie over INR20 lakh crore over about 10 years.
IRFC plans to act as sole financing arm and aggregator, with talks under way with the World Bank, other multilaterals and domestic players; model expected in place by end FY27.
Employee headcount roughly doubled in the last year, per the CEO.
demand_pricing: Floating-rate exposure: repo rate up 25 bps and back-to-back TONAR up 25 bps; management says it passes these through on non-railway loans and that resets are both ways.
Yen borrowing: about USD2 billion raised last year at around 1.8%, now about 2.25% after TONAR increases; hedging cost stated as not above 6.3%.
Term loans from banks are about 25% of the borrowing mix; management claims a 20-30 bps cushion against rate moves.
Prepayment: management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no floor on benchmark-linked pricing, and lowest-in-market cost of funds.
Overhead cost cited at about INR0.15 per unit of lending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities, and what are the main risks on railway capex, asset growth or funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 disbursements will exceed FY26, with non-IR pipeline (metros, ports, renewables, thermal, Gencos, roads) ready for Q3 or early Q4. Railway-linked funding is to start from FY28 at a minimum of INR50,000 crore a year, with the aggregator model to be set by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key financial risks (NIM, borrowing costs, asset quality) in a changing rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO cited a 6.55% WACC, lower than other NBFCs, and a push to raise more 54EC bonds and ECB. Management said the ALM team monitors margins weekly and keeps a minimum spread of INR0.85-0.90 on non-railway loans.

qa_highlights.question: How is non-railway lending priced, and how fast can rate increases be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans are priced on a cost-plus basis, and floating-rate loans reset monthly, quarterly or yearly. Management said a 25 bps repo hike and TONAR increase were passed through, and the company keeps a 20-30 bps cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there prepayment pressure, as seen at other government lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no benchmark floor, and the cheapest funding in the market. Some prepayments by borrowers into IRFC were said to be business wins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM and disbursement vision, and is the INR5 lakh crore AUM target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated near INR5 lakh crore AUM by end FY27 (possibly 1,000-2,000 crore short), up from INR4.85 lakh crore at end FY26. It targets a 60:40 railway-to-diversified mix by 2030 and near-10% PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share price move so much, and what are the dividend and value prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share price moves are outside its control and pointed to fundamentals. It cited an interim dividend of INR1.15 this year against INR1.05 last year, and a payout of about 40% of profit over the last two years.

543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.

The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.
Management said the competitive intensity has moderated over the last couple of quarters; it sees no change in behaviour since JSW's acquisition of Akzo.
Differentiated products make up about 30% of sales and are described as price-inelastic, so margin reduction is expected mainly in the other two-thirds of the portfolio.
Premium emulsions are a growing share; management said value growth has exceeded volume growth in almost all categories over the last 20 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company pursuing more aggressive market share gains, and will a 200bp gross margin sacrifice be enough to reach about 24% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board judged the company had been too conservative on margins; it will spend more on trade schemes and influencers, lowering gross margin 2-2.5pp while EBITDA margin should hold. Management said yes, 24% growth is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the gross margin reduction come from, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra spend will be netted from revenue through trade discounts and influencer costs, mainly in non-differentiated products. Management said competitive intensity has normalised and the move reflects a wish to grow faster, not a response to competitors.

qa_highlights.answer: Gross sales grew double-digit in each of the last five months, but higher trade and influencer discounts cut Q4 net growth to 8.5%. Management does not expect net sales growth to fall back to single digits.

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation worsens. It said the company now acts independently on pricing and that margins should normalise by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 1 and Tier 2 coverage is now good, and growth will come from deeper dealer throughput, not city size; with about 19,500 dealers it sees room to double sales per dealer.

543258|2026-06.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.
543258|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR350 crore, with double-digit volume and value growth across all four product categories. EBITDA rose 42% to INR61.9 crore (margin 17.7% vs 14.8%), and PAT rose 60.7% to INR42.4 crore, helped partly by a mark-to-market treasury gain. Consolidated revenue was INR369.7 crore (+19.7%), but subsidiary Apple Chemie's margins were compressed by high-cost inventory and limited B2B pass-through. Management said it will spend more aggressively on trade and influencers in Q2 to widen the growth gap versus the industry, and that the Jodhpur capex cycle is complete.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

543259|2026-03.headline: Home First Q4 FY26: record Q4 disbursement of INR1,572 crore (+23.5% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR540 crore (+41.4% YoY); FY27 AUM growth guided ~25%.
543259|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 saw record quarterly disbursement, PAT of INR149 crore (+42.7% YoY, +6.6% QoQ), and AUM of INR15,878 crore (+24.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ). Management guided to ~25% AUM growth in FY27, a 5%-5.25% spread and 30-40bps credit cost, and said there is no visible impact yet from the Middle East conflict.

543259|2026-06.headline: Home First Q1 FY27: AUM up 25.7% YoY to INR16,938 crore and PAT up 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, with stable asset quality.

543271|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue hit an all-time high of INR1,394 crore (up 24% YoY) and EBITDA rose 51% YoY to INR221 crore, the highest in three years, with PAT up 60% YoY to INR111 crore. H1 revenue grew 25% and EBITDA 44% YoY. Management reiterated its FY27 guidance of INR750-800 crore (EBITDA basis as discussed on the call) and said it expects to land closer to the upper end, helped by a recent European competitor plant closure in acetic anhydride. Uncertainty remains on the large innovator CDMO contract, where future volume visibility is still pending.

543273|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose to ₹256 crore (from ~₹201 crore) with ~38% EBITDA margin, but Q4 revenue dipped as ~₹60 crore slipped into Q1 FY27.

Order inflow of ₹1,075 crore was the highest in company history, with an order book of about ₹1,400 crore spanning dredging, charter hire and shipbuilding. Q4 margins were weak (~27% as stated by an analyst) because JNPA and Pondicherry contracts were single-payment on completion and their revenue (~₹60 crore) is expected in Q1 FY27. Management guided to ~30% revenue growth for FY27 and FY28 and a 35–40% EBITDA margin, and outlined a ₹400–500 crore FY27 capex plan.

543275|2026-03.headline: Anupam FY26 consolidated revenue rose 65% to INR2,384 crores, with Q4 PAT of INR56 crores versus INR63 crores a year earlier.

Exit RoA guided at about 1.4-1.5%; PAT of about INR300 crores for FY27 reiterated, with guidance not revised upward.
Retail-to-IF mix of 45-55 kept as a medium-term target; management does not expect to reach it by year-end FY27.
Monthly IF disbursement run-rate of INR450-550 crores targeted over next 5 months as about 50 branches are added; October at INR450-475 crores.
FY28 guidance to be given with Q4 results; management expects at least mid-level of 30-35% growth to continue.
Tier 2 balance of INR200 crores targeted by December or by Q4 FY27; another CRAR uplift of 1.8-2% expected.
capex_capacity: About 50 new branches planned over the next 4-5 months; about 10 already opened, with contribution of INR50-60 lakhs per branch and about INR30 crores of disbursement expected from new branches by February.

Tier 2 raise of INR200 crores in first week of October; a further INR200 crores (INR100 crores approved by board) to be raised, timing dependent on rate stabilisation.
NABARD variable-rate borrowing of INR1,200 crores taken at about 8.5%, now about 7.5%; treasury evaluating switch to fixed rate.
demand_pricing: Credit demand healthy system-wide; deposit mobilisation competitive with credit outpacing deposits. Management says funding costs are back in focus after the rate environment shifted.

Paying-book yield for Q2 was a little above 17.5% (Q1 cited 17.4%); MFI yield about 25.8%; management expects similar range for next two quarters.
Gross write-off of INR591 crores, almost entirely JLG and individual loans (IL) under CGFMU cover; retail write-off about INR3 crores.
Q2 disbursements into IF about INR450 crores per month; IBPC renewal expected at rates below 5% for six-month money.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CGFMU guarantee cover currently active, and what provision is being made for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Cover for FY27 disbursements has not opened as the central government must notify renewal; bank is providing about INR40-45 crores in H1 for premiums (about 1-1.5% fees, INR70-80 crores expected). Disbursements up to 31 March 2026 are fully covered and renewed.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure and collections in drought-hit districts?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crores of exposure in affected Karnataka and Maharashtra areas, nearly all CGFMU-covered except about 3% (INR300-350 crores of last-six-month disbursements not yet covered). September and October collections stable; management expects a possible lagged impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 growth and the PAT guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances growth guidance of 30-35% maintained; PAT of about INR300 crores still achievable, supported by the digital/CLOU business. Q2 PAT of INR76.5 crores is similar to Q1 despite lower PSLC income.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to NIM and cost-to-income going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM expected to be broadly stable with marginal improvement as MFI share rises; CTI of 70.5-70.6% reported, about 68.6% net of partner payouts. CGFMU cost shave-off not significant.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 slippage split, and what caused the rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 slippages of INR122 crores, about INR65 crores in IF and the rest in secured and digital; CV slips in a few accounts. Management views normal IF slippages at INR50-60 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Tier 1 or capital optimisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to IBPC and fixed-rate NABARD refinancing; Tier 1 comfort zone cited as about 20%, moving to 18.5-19% for CRAR. Further Tier 2 raise planned before year-end.

risks_watch: CGFMU cover renewal: fresh-disbursement cover not yet open for FY27; if delayed, Q3 provisioning and P&L could be affected.

Funding cost pressure: deposit mobilisation competitive, short-end rates volatile; Tier 2 raise timing uncertain.
CLOU credit quality: new product scaling to INR500-600 crores; management says one year of track record is needed before drawing conclusions.
IF share of advances at about 41% vs 45-55 retail/IF guidance; reaching target depends on IF growth outpacing retail.

543280|2026-03.headline: Nazara FY26 EBITDA rose 66% to INR 255 crore, with Q4 EBITDA margin at 19.5%, helped by a one-time INR 31 crore Rusk Media gain.
543280|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue was INR 1,829 crore (up 13% YoY) and EBITDA INR 255 crore (up 66%), a record, with EBITDA margin at 13.9%. Q4 revenue was INR 398 crore and EBITDA INR 78 crore (19.5% margin). Gaming rose to 90% of EBITDA in FY26 from 56% in FY25. Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition was completed in the quarter but will be consolidated only from Q1 FY27, pending Spanish FDI approval expected in 3-4 weeks. Management guided to growth in revenue and EBITDA for FY27 without numerical guidance.

segments.name: PC and console publishing (Curve Games, Fusebox, Human Fall Flat)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 261 crore and EBITDA INR 101 crore (39% margin). Human Fall Flat crossed 58 million lifetime units. Analyst noted revenue growth was hardly visible YoY; management said the company had a low signing period before the acquisition.

segments.name: Offline gaming (Smaaash, Funky Monkeys)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 99 crore and EBITDA INR 27 crore, profitable in the year. Funky Monkeys footprint expanding; Smaaash 2.0 format in progress.

segments.commentary: Revenue and EBITDA each grew 32% YoY in FY26, but Q4 revenue declined sequentially, which management attributed to exiting traditional adtech and UK new-homes market weakness.

segments.name: Sportskeeda
segments.commentary: Remained profitable in FY26 despite Google Core update traffic losses; analyst cited revenue down about 38% in FY26. Management expects margin improvement in FY27 on a smaller base.

segments.name: NODWIN (associate)
segments.commentary: EBITDA swung to INR 21 crore profit in FY26 from INR 14 crore loss in FY25. Q4 associate losses included a INR 50 crore goodwill write-off on OML assets, mainly NH7 Weekender. Planning to raise USD 100-200 million and an independent IPO.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance; management expects growth in both revenue and EBITDA in FY27, with operating leverage from COEs and AI.

Bluetile consolidation from Q1 FY27 once Spanish FDI approval is received (expected in 3-4 weeks). Management said pro forma EBITDA would at least double if combined with Bluetile's CY25 EBITDA of INR 254 crore.
Curve Games expects at least 6 new releases in FY27, maybe more; margin target of 50% on signed games.
Fusebox plans three Big Brother seasons and a Traitors launch in FY27, plus three new Love Island seasons.
Non-core divestments (NODWIN, Sportskeeda or adtech) possible in FY27-FY28; management said there is no rush.
