Smaaash 2.0 re-imagined format in progress; Funky Monkeys footprint expanding.
Animal Jam: first Mattel Monster High IP integration launched in Q1 FY27; Roblox native experience planned; a new hyper-casual game for kids and women in North America is due in Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Bluetile operates in casual evergreen (solitaire, word games, board and puzzle games) and hybrid casual. Management cited Triple Dot (valued over USD 1 billion) and Easybrain (acquired by Miniclip for about USD 1 billion) as comparables.
Management said platform commissions (Google, Apple at 30%) are coming down over time, which should aid margins.
Adtech decline reflects a deliberate shift from traditional adtech to the DSP product Vizibl; UK new-homes market weakness hit Space and Time's Q4 discretionary spend.
Fusebox revenue is seasonal; Q3 FY26 fell about 49% QoQ before recovering in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR 51 crore other income and what explains the NODWIN associate loss of about INR 31 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income included a one-time INR 31 crore gain on Rusk Media from a revaluation after its new funding round, plus currency gains on loans to Nazara UK and mutual fund gains. The associate loss reflected a INR 50 crore NODWIN goodwill write-off on OML assets and Moonshine losses.

qa_highlights.question: Is Sportskeeda's decline recoverable, or should margins be modelled at 12-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has not yet come through; the focus in FY26 was protecting EBITDA over revenue. Cost optimisation continues and margins are expected to rise in FY27 on a smaller base. Pro Football Network and PrimeTimer are showing positive signs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NODWIN fundraising and IPO plan, and will Nazara monetise its stake?
qa_highlights.answer: NODWIN plans to raise USD 100-200 million, a mix of primary and secondary, and prepare an independent IPO as soon as timing is right. Nazara will consider monetising non-core assets (NODWIN, Sportskeeda or adtech) but is in no hurry.

qa_highlights.question: What is Bluetile's TAM and scalability, and what is the FY27 growth and margin outlook post consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Bluetile's casual evergreen and hybrid casual segments were described as large and profitable with global reach. Management gave no specific guidance but pointed to Bluetile CY25 revenue of INR 1,460 crore and EBITDA of INR 254 crore, with combined EBITDA at least doubling pro forma.

qa_highlights.question: Why did adtech revenue decline sequentially in Q4, and is it temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was partly deliberate, exiting traditional adtech, and partly UK new-homes market weakness hitting Space and Time. Space and Time finished FY26 ahead of AOP and management expects FY27 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Can Curve Games margins hold above 30-35% as Switch 2 launches scale, and when will Bluetile consolidate?
qa_highlights.answer: Curve targets 50% margin on signed games and expects margins to hold. Bluetile is expected to close after Spanish FDI approval in 3-4 weeks and consolidate from Q1 FY27.

Sportskeeda is still hit by Google Core update traffic losses; FY26 revenue fell about 38% per analyst.

Gaming contribution to EBITDA increased from 56% in FY '25 to 90% in FY '26, as we strengthened our focus on building a high -margin, globally diversified gaming platform across mobile, PC, and console, and offline gaming.

543280|2026-06.headline: Nazara Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore; Bluetile/BestPlay acquisition restructured to $303 million all-cash.
543280|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore driven by associate losses (about INR 62 crore share of loss) and impairment, mainly on the Moonshine remnant value. Excluding NODWIN's deconsolidation, comparable revenue grew about 9% YoY. Gaming revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 275 crore at a 19.5% EBITDA margin, with heavier user acquisition spend compressing margins at Bluetile, Kiddopia and Curve. Management restructured the Bluetile and BestPlay deal to a fixed $303 million all-cash price, with $89 million at closing and $214 million by 1 April 2027, and named Bluetile founder Raymond Stauffer as Nazara CEO from 1 September 2026.

segments.name: Kiddopia / Animal Jam
segments.commentary: Kiddopia revenue grew 19% YoY on higher UA spend with 24-month LTV/CAC trending up; Animal Jam revenue grew 11% YoY.

segments.name: Fusebox Games
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 82 crore, up 12% YoY; Love Island ranked #1 in free apps and #5 in top-grossing apps in the US. Big Brother and The Traitors are the next growth drivers.

segments.name: Curve Games (PC and Console publishing)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 53 crore and EBITDA INR 14 crore (27% margin), down from about 40% last financial year; more than 60% of development spend went to new signings and releases start from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Offline gaming (SMAAASH, Funky Monkeys)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 34 crore and EBITDA INR 11 crore (33% margin); Funky Monkeys revenue grew 58% YoY. SMAAASH 2.0 first reinvention targeted at Lower Parel, Mumbai, in Q4 FY27.

segments.commentary: Datawrkz revenue INR 126 crore with EBITDA INR 3 crore. Management said 60-80% of AdTech revenue is pass-through, so revenue growth does not translate directly into EBITDA.

segments.name: Absolute Sports (Sportskeeda, Pro Football Network)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 28 crore and EBITDA INR 1 crore; Sportskeeda turned EBITDA positive on lower costs, and Pro Football Network posted a 19% EBITDA margin versus break-even in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: NODWIN Gaming
segments.commentary: Q1 is the seasonally weakest quarter with stable revenue and losses substantially lower YoY; organic growth target 30%+ for FY27, with IPO readiness in progress and Comic Con expanding to 14 Indian events.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jawar (AK Investment) asked Bluetile's founder journey and whether growth was organic or inorganic, and what skin in the game Raymond Stauffer would have under the all-cash deal.
qa_highlights.answer: Raymond was not on the call; Maxime Loppin said Bluetile's growth is not organic in the sense of inorganic M&A but is driven by paid UA, with spend based on campaign ROI on new games and features. On incentives, Nitish Mittersain said a structure to incentivise management including Raymond would be communicated over the next few days, with the fundraise not discussed before Board approval.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Patel (Equirus) asked about the Curve Games release slate, margin trajectory, and offline capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Susan Planck said releases start with Sovereign Tower (this week), Dragon Shelter (September 2026) and more unannounced titles before year-end; Q1 27% margin is below the ~40% of last year and new signings should lift later quarters. Nitish Mittersain said offline commitment across SMAAASH and Funky Monkeys is about INR 50 crore, with SMAAASH 2.0 Lower Parel launch expected January-March 2027 and no further capital decided until product-market fit.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Patel asked about NODWIN's IPO progress and whether a NODWIN secondary sale would fund the Bluetile consideration.
qa_highlights.answer: Akshat Rathee said Comic Con expands from 11 shows last year to 14 domestic plus 2-3 international, and pre-IPO interest is strong. Nitish Mittersain said funding options include about $20 million of cash on Bluetile's balance sheet, internal cash flow, debt, equity and stake sales, without confirming a NODWIN secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Bajaj (Choice) asked whether the EBITDA margin decline would normalise quickly, why Bluetile margin fell, D&A outlook, and the timing of the $214 million tranches.
qa_highlights.answer: Nitish Mittersain said margins are deferred as UA is expensed upfront with no caps while LTV/CAC guardrails hold; Bluetile's Q1 margin is about 11% versus 17.6% a year ago. D&A outside Bluetile is steady; Bluetile's amortisation was not quantified. Anupriya Sinha Das said about $75 million is due in 90 days, about $35 million in December 2026, and the balance before 1 April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital) asked why the payment was front-loaded and funded by debt or dilution, whether tax liability arises from real-money gaming notices, and the reason for the ~INR 62 crore associate loss.
qa_highlights.answer: Nitish Mittersain cited performance-based payouts that could reach 180% of committed amounts, misalignment in CEO metrics, and full cash accrual to Nazara instead of 50% leakage to founders. Tax exposure was said to be limited to the investments, which are fully written off. The associate loss was mainly write-offs of remnant Moonshine value after recent judgments, with about 90% already written down earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Jain (Dolat) asked about Nitish's changed role, Fusebox growth outlook, Sportskeeda recovery, and AdTech margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Nitish said Raymond will run day-to-day operations while he focuses on strategy, M&A and technology. Nitish expects Fusebox's Big Brother and The Traitors to drive the next step-change, without giving a growth figure. Mayank Kumar said Q1 was in line with internal expectations and revenue should rise in Q2-Q4 with the US sports season. Rohit Sharma said AdTech margins are investment-led and that 60-80% of AdTech revenue is pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavik Shah (Invexa) asked for Bluetile's sustainable margins, full-year outlook, and Nazara-level guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Maxime Loppin said Q1 margin was about 11% against 17.6% in Q1 FY26, with flexibility to raise EBITDA later and no firm quarterly revenue pattern. Nitish Mittersain said no Nazara-level revenue, EBITDA or margin guidance at this point.

qa_highlights.question: Manan Poladia (MKP) asked for Badlands Crew and Dragon Shelter sales and how the new titles compare with Human: Fall Flat.
qa_highlights.answer: Susan Planck said Badlands Crew has sold about 50,000-60,000 copies, in line with expectations. Dragon Shelter has about 130,000 Steam wishlists, above expectations. Susan said results would not match Human: Fall Flat (60 million units), and the two upcoming releases have no in-app purchase forecast.

543283|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, with same-store sales growth of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.1%.

Growth was volume-led (dine-in transactions up 63.5%) with no price increase taken. Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% from about 5.5% in Q4 and roughly 350 bps higher YoY, helped by a 130 bps sequential gross margin recovery in Barbeque Nation India. International gross margin fell on Middle East-linked food inflation, and net debt rose marginally to INR106 crores.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 46.6%, SSSG 8.5%, dine-in volume growth 45.2%, gross profit up 40.3%. Restaurant operating margin 18.7%, but gross margin down ~3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation; added 1 UAE restaurant.

segments.name: Premium casual dining (Premium CDR)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth ~36%, SSSG 13.6%, dine-in volume growth ~40%. Mature restaurants deliver restaurant operating margin of upwards of 20%; added 1 and closed 1 restaurant, network unchanged. Q4 FY26 cohort expected to lift segment margin.

guidance_outlook: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 as comparables tighten, with Q3 and Q4 FY27 lapping the strongest quarter of FY26; management called this a base effect, not weaker demand.

Margin levers for FY27: gross margin recovery in India, mature portfolio ROM expansion, new-store cohort maturation and back-end cost leverage; management did not give a pre-Ind AS double-digit EBITDA margin timeline.
Target of 300 restaurants by FY27 (about 40 additions this year vs ~35 last year); 15 restaurants under construction to operationalise in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR140 crores (INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores maintenance and ancillary), per the prior guidance reiterated on the call.
Management sees Barbeque Nation India capable of ~600 restaurants at current scale, up from an earlier view of 400-450, given the Big Buffet format in Tier 2/3 markets.
Momentum said to be continuing into July; revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, and the quarter ended at about INR425 crores.
capex_capacity: Restaurant count closed Q1 FY27 at 266 after 5 additions; target of 300 by FY27 maintained.

demand_pricing: Growth described as entirely volume-led; no price increase taken in Q1 despite inflation. Average per-cover spend declined due to value initiatives from Q2 FY26 and has now stabilised at Q4 FY26 levels.
Average revenue per mature restaurant is around INR7 crores; management has not given a target for the next step.
Repeat business is ~45-47% of the base, with the new-vs-repeat mix shifting slightly toward new guests. Average bill is ~4.3 pax, and repeat tracking relies on one mobile number per bill.

Delivery growth of 62% was supported by value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar brands and by higher marketing spend. Delivery share of mix rose ~2 pp YoY and carries commission and packaging costs of about 30%.
Management described the mature cost base as 'normalised' after recent hires in culinary, marketing and digital; each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost impact.

543287|2026-03.headline: Lodha FY26 presales INR205bn (+16%) and PAT INR34.3bn (20% margin); FY27 presales guided to INR240bn, PAT growth ~20% medium term.
543287|2026-03.overview: Lodha delivered its best-ever quarter in Q4 FY26 with presales of about INR58.9bn (+23% YoY), and full-year presales of INR205bn (+16%) with every quarter a record. PAT grew 24% to INR34.3bn, with PAT margin touching 20% for the first time, while adjusted EBITDA grew 14% and the embedded development margin held near 33%. Management shifted its primary guidance metric to PAT, guiding FY27 presales of about INR240bn (mid-teens growth) and PAT growth of about 20% CAGR to over INR85bn by FY31. Business development was strong, with 12 projects and INR600bn GDV added, and net debt fell to 0.23x equity.

segments.commentary: Contributed about INR24bn presales in FY26, over 12% of total, three years after pilot entry in FY23.

segments.commentary: Annuity income about INR3bn in FY26 from 3.8mn sq ft complete of 8.8mn sq ft pipeline; target about INR10bn annual rent by FY31 excluding data centres.

qa_highlights.question: How ready is the FY27 INR218bn launch pipeline and what is the status of environmental clearances?

qa_highlights.question: Palava residential outlook for FY27 with road infrastructure completion?

qa_highlights.answer: Construction cost up 3-5%, margin impact nominal; labour attrition 5-10% above seasonal norms, viewed as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Own data centre vs monetising land?

543287|2026-06.headline: Lodha Q1 FY27 PAT more than doubled to INR 13.7 billion (26.9% margin) on land sales, while pre-sales rose only 4% to INR 46.3 billion.
543287|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 43% YoY to INR 50 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to INR 21.5 billion at a 43% margin, with PAT of INR 13.7 billion versus INR 6.8 billion a year ago. Management said the quarter was flattered by roughly half of the year's planned land sales, including data centre park land sold to Digital Edge India at about INR 420 million per acre. Residential pre-sales were deliberately weak because about one-third of normal launches were postponed to Q2 on Middle East conflict concerns. Net debt fell by INR 4.5 billion to under INR 50 billion, with net debt to equity at about 0.2x.

segments.name: Residential (DevCo)
segments.commentary: Pre-sales of INR 46.3 billion with only one Mumbai launch (about 0.4 million sq ft); sustenance sales drove the quarter. Premium and luxury made up almost 60% of sales, and mid-income (below INR 3 crore) about 50% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Land sales
segments.commentary: Data centre and other land pre-sales of about INR 12 billion, with PAT contribution of about INR 6 billion. Management guides land sales of INR 20-30 billion a year for the next several years.

segments.name: Annuity / RentCo
segments.commentary: June exit run-rate of about INR 3 billion with no data centre contribution. Target is over INR 30 billion by FY32, including about INR 20 billion-plus from data centres, INR 6 billion from retail and office, and INR 4 billion from warehousing and industrial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of about 20% growth on INR 34.3 billion, i.e. about INR 41 billion; Q1 delivered 33% of this. Management said 20% is an annual target and warned against annualising the quarter.
FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 240 billion reaffirmed, with H1 at 40-42% of the full year. Q2 pre-sales expected at INR 50 billion or more, with July off to a good start.
Embedded margin excluding land sales was in the early 30s; full-year margin guidance of 32-34% retained, with no expectation of margins in the 40s.
Medium-term PAT growth of about 20% a year, taking PAT beyond INR 85 billion by FY31; ROE expected to move toward 20% from about 16% in FY26 but may not reach it.
DevCo to be net debt-free within 2-3 years; net debt to equity to stay below the 0.5x ceiling.
Pricing to rise 5-7% across micro markets over the year, with room for a further 100-200 bps.
Dividend policy of 15-20% of PAT, then debt reduction, then buyback or special dividend.
capex_capacity: Data centre park: about 660 acres at Palava, with about 3 GW of power tie-up, 5 fibre routes and 5 transmission lines. About 130 acres of the first 370-acre phase is sold; about 150 more acres are to be sold over 3-4 years at about INR 600 million per acre (about INR 90 billion).

Plan to build about 1 GW of powered shell on about 90 acres, generating over INR 20 billion of annual rent by FY32. Leasing of the first box is targeted within FY27, with physical work on the company's own box to start in calendar 2026.
Estimated capex for the power-shell infrastructure is INR 500-700 crore over time, per the CFO-level answer on infrastructure.
Power density is 11-15 MW per acre. Management does not yet plan chips or racks and sees turnkey shell at least two years away.
demand_pricing: Middle East NRI buyers are about 4-5% of sales. Management sees the impact as moderate and expects NRI and US-based buyers to shift some money toward Indian homes.
Construction cost: if energy-linked inflation persists for a full year, management expects a 1-1.5% rise in project cost (35-75 bps project EBITDA impact). Supply chain is about 95% domestic.
Conversion rate reportedly 8% or higher from July, with a long-run aim of 10%.
Sales from new cities (Pune, Bangalore, NCR, MMR) to reach 30-45% of pre-sales in the medium term.

Palava land sale price rose to about INR 420 million per acre from about INR 210 million in calendar 2025. Management puts fair market value at about INR 650 million per acre, reachable in about 18 months.
Competition described as rational. Branded share of MMR is about 30%, which management expects to reach 40-45% by the end of the decade.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value and margin of the land sales in the quarter, and how much did they add to PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore of land pre-sales including data centre land, with revenue recognised at 85-90% of that. PAT contribution was about INR 600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the data centre rental estimate appear to fall from INR 30 billion to INR 20 billion-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change. The INR 30 billion FY32 target is unchanged, and data centres account for INR 20 billion-plus of it. Powered shell rent is a little over INR 20 million per MW a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the pre-sales guidance factor in the Middle East war, and is there upside if it ends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been contained and the guidance is maintained. It will review once the conflict ends. MMR high-value sales have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any margin outlook beyond the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Embedded margins excluding land were in the early 30s. Management said the 40s-level margin was driven by forward-loaded land sales and that the full-year guidance of early 30s stands.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed per acre for a data centre land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost is about 10-15% of the sales price, and the CFO put group infrastructure capex at INR 500-700 crore over time. Most of the sale price flows through to cash after tax.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company compete with its data centre buyers, and what is its competitive edge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company offers powered shell, which no other provider offers, and that its advantages are land, power, recycled water, ecosystem and relationships.

risks_watch: Pre-sales were up only 4% YoY; the FY27 target of INR 240 billion requires H2 weighting, with about INR 250 billion of GDV in the launch calendar.
Land sales are lumpy and drove a large share of PAT; the 20% PAT growth target is annual, so quarterly results will vary.
Middle East conflict is prolonged. Energy-linked construction cost inflation could reach 1-1.5% if it lasts a full year.

543308|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR 1,075 crore, but EBITDA pre-Ind AS fell 33.5% to INR 131 crore as new hospitals dragged margins.
543308|2026-03.overview: KIMS reported Q4 FY26 total revenue of INR 1,084 crore (+35.3% YoY, +8.1% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 216 crore (+6.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 19.9% versus 25.3% a year ago. Management attributed the margin compression to roughly INR 32 crore of EBITDA erosion from newer units (in operation under one year), while mature units held about 28.5-29% margins. PAT fell to INR 33 crore from INR 106 crore a year ago. Management is raising about INR 1,500 crore via QIP to cut net debt, which it says has peaked at INR 3,000-plus crore, and targets net debt to EBITDA of 1-2x from about 1x-3x currently.

segments.name: Mature units
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 862 crore with EBITDA about INR 250 crore, a margin of roughly 28.5-29%. For FY26, mature units generated INR 3,335 crore revenue and about INR 956 crore EBITDA, about 29.5% margin.

segments.name: Newer units (under one year old)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 224 crore with EBITDA erosion of about INR 32 crore. For FY26, these units generated INR 597 crore revenue and about INR 128 crore EBITDA erosion.

segments.name: Mahadevapura (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 49 crore and loss about INR 14 crore; management says it averages about INR 17 crore/month and targets INR 25-30 crore/month over 12 months.

segments.name: Electronic City / PES (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 17 crore with loss about INR 25 crore; commissioned in December 2025. Management expects EBITDA-positive by end of FY27.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 47 crore and loss about INR 5 crore. Management says Thane was EBITDA-neutral in March and April 2026, before adding doctors in May.

segments.name: Nashik
segments.commentary: Q4 loss about INR 1 crore. Still awaiting STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA empanelment.

guidance_outlook: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth guided at about 10-12% in FY27, below historical rates due to Kondapur and Kompally.
Newer-unit combined losses in FY27 and FY28 expected to be less than half of the roughly INR 120-128 crore FY26 drag, subject to insurance empanelments.
Use about INR 1,000 crore of QIP proceeds to retire debt; remainder for losses and capex in existing facilities.

Palakkad (300-bed, acquired; consolidated) expected at INR 6.5-7 crore revenue in May 2026 with about 5% negative EBITDA, breakeven by June-July 2026, targeting INR 12-15 crore/month revenue over time.
Bangalore ARPOB to be modelled at INR 75,000 annually; Andhra ARPOB at about INR 26,000-27,000.
Bengaluru occupancy expected at 35-40% by end of FY27 on full bed capacity.
Kondapur move to new 800-bed facility from first week of June 2026; Phase 1 of 400-500 beds; INR 50-75 crore further capex deferred to FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: New Kondapur (Hyderabad) 800-bed hospital; shift from old facility starting first week of June 2026, with a one-month transition and old facility possibly running 2-3 months more.
Phase 1 of Kondapur to open at 400-500 beds; remaining 300 beds to be commissioned as occupancy rises.

Expansions in FY26: Kompally (Hyderabad), two in Guntur, Thane and Sangli (Maharashtra), Mahadevapura and Electronic City (Bengaluru), Kollam (Kerala), and fertility centres in Hyderabad and Guntur. KIMS Cuddles mother-and-child unit opened in Nellore; cancer block opened in Ongole.

Greenfield projects planned in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu (one hospital), with continued expansion in Andhra and Telangana; these take 3-5 years to commission. Secunderabad expansion expected within 18 months.
Project funding norm: about 40% equity and 65% debt. Doctor participation typically 3-5% of equity; the model remains open.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per operating bed rose 13.7% YoY and 1.7% QoQ in Q4; average revenue per patient up 14% YoY and 3.5% QoQ.
IP volumes up 17.9% YoY and 4% QoQ; OP volumes up 30.1% YoY and 4.1% QoQ in Q4. FY26 IP volumes +15.4%, OP +25.4%.
Maharashtra Q4 occupancy at 60.5% (FY26 about 52.1%), which management calls the new base.
Hyderabad is the most competitive market; 4-5 hospitals commissioned in the last year. Management reports losing only one or two doctors, with no material attrition.
Insurance empanelment delays (new GIC common empanelment process and volume of new hospitals) are the main ramp-up constraint for new units.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise a INR 1,500 crore QIP after saying debt had peaked, and are new expansion plans firm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is near INR 3,000-plus crore and the QIP will retire debt, with cash flow then funding 3-5 year greenfield projects. Expansion plans are still being explored; 400-500 beds of small acquisitions may come in the next two quarters, all in home markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on insurance empanelment for the new hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Nashik still needs STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA. Thane has GIPSA, with Medi Assist and STAR nearly done, covering about 70% of insurance volume. Bangalore needs 3-4 more months. Confusion from the new GIC common-empanelment process caused the delays.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARPOB and occupancy run-rates for Bangalore and Andhra Pradesh for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore ARPOB of about INR 85,000 for FY26 but management says to model INR 75,000. Andhra at about INR 26,000-27,000 in Q3 and Q4. Bengaluru occupancy expected 35-40% by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kondapur capex and phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The 800-bed Kondapur facility is almost fully capex-complete, with INR 50-75 crore left for two additional floors in FY28-FY29. Phase 1 covers 400-500 beds. Transition cost is expected to be about INR 15-25 crore, based on the Sunshine move precedent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for FY27 after the QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of debt to be retired from QIP proceeds. The balance covers losses at new hospitals and capex in existing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA growth is expected for the Telangana cluster in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth of about 10-12% in FY27, below historical levels because of the Kondapur and Kompally commissioning.

risks_watch: Insurance empanelment delays at Nashik, Thane and Bangalore hospitals, which management says limit ramp-up.
Margin dilution from new units: cluster-level margins, not company-level, are the guided metric; Q4 company margin was 19.9%.
Leverage: management targets net debt/EBITDA of 1-2x; the call says the current ratio is about 1x-3x (ambiguous). The QIP is about INR 1,500 crore.
Q4 PAT of INR 33 crore and EPS decline of 37.2% in FY26, with management acknowledging ROE and ROCE have fallen.
Geopolitical and macro risk: management cited the Gulf war and a government austerity appeal.
Competition for doctors in Hyderabad; possible common-empanelment initiative by IRDAI/GIC, which management declined to comment on.
Inconsistencies in disclosures: bed-addition plan changed without a timeline; management said the update would come next quarter.
543308|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and cluster-level margin trajectory, but cautious on near-term profitability, acknowledging that new-unit losses and insurance empanelment delays will persist. Management was evasive on forward-looking growth numbers and on the common-empanelment policy.
key_quotes: Expansion has no meaning without clinical excellence and excellence is incomplete without empathy.
As long as we are able to grow that on a quarter-on-quarter basis, that is the direction we should look at.
Right now, the only challenge I see is the insurance empanelment.

543308|2026-06.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.
543308|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total revenue of INR 1,196 crore (+36.1% YoY, +10.3% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 240 crore at a 20.1% margin, with PAT of INR 37 crore versus INR 85 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by IP volumes (+26.6% YoY) and OP volumes (+28.5% YoY), with the Kondapur hospital commissioned in June and Palakkad (Kerala) opened. The QIP raised INR 1,500 crore, of which INR 1,100-1,125 crore repaid debt, and a INR 600 crore promoter preferential allotment is partly pending. Management guided Telangana to 30-35% margins over time, Kerala to 20-22% in two to three years, and Bengaluru to break-even for the full year, while several new units are still ramping up.

segments.commentary: Management said revenue and EBITDA grew strongly YoY in Telangana and Andhra; Kondapur did INR 45 crore in July (first full month) against INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Telangana occupancy is about 61% on the adjusted bed base excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura reached EBITDA break-even in June and did about INR 20 crore revenue in July; Electronic City expected to break even in about one to two quarters. Management aims for zero EBITDA for the cluster for FY27. Census-bed occupancy at Mahadevapura is about 40%.

segments.name: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik, Nagpur)
segments.commentary: Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly revenue in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% EBITDA margin. Nashik reached EBITDA break-even in Q1; Nagpur did INR 30 crore revenue in July. Empanelment delays of four to five months weighed on Q1.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Kerala margins are in the single digits currently, with management expecting mid-teens in FY28 and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Palakkad opened, taking Kerala to three units; one more hospital (Thrissur) is due in three to four months.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management said AP remains strong. Q1 ARPOB growth slowed from prior quarters (Q4 FY26 about INR 27,000), which management attributed to seasonal case mix. Cancer services were added to most AP hospitals in the last two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Telangana EBITDA margin expected to return to 30-35% over time as new Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ramp up; management said 30% is achievable by FY30 without new beds, and 70% occupancy is targeted in three to four years.
Bengaluru cluster targeted at zero EBITDA for full FY27; Bengaluru ARPOB expected to settle at INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, versus about INR 90,000+ recently.
Kondapur full potential of about INR 100 crore revenue per month (about INR 1,200 crore a year) within four to five years; model margin around 30%, with 30-32% suggested for the next two years.
ARPOB growth guidance of 4-5% per year; management called 15-16% historical growth too aggressive to model.
Maintenance capex about INR 100 crore per year for three to four years; about INR 100-125 crore growth capex over the next nine months, including Rajahmundry construction (INR 60-75 crore in FY27).
Debt-equity intended to be kept around 2.5:1; surplus cash to go to greenfield and brownfield growth in core states. Minority interest about 10.5% currently, 10-15% longer term.
Empanelment with the remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, expected by end-August to mid-September 2026.
capex_capacity: Kondapur hospital commissioned in June 2026 (first patient 20 June); about 450-500 operational beds added in the last 10 days of Q1, and the old Kondapur hospital will run for about six more months with rent of about INR 90 lakh per month plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year of operating cost.

Palakkad (Kerala) opened in Q1; Thrissur to commence in three to four months; Electronic City and other Bengaluru beds added at Mahadevapura (operational beds up from about 170 to 210, total cluster 280 to 340).
Secunderabad: old 250-bed facility demolished; replacement facility expected by end of next year.

Two O&M agreements (Golden Lan Solutions, Sarvottam Healthcare) approved in draft: a 300-bed Telangana hospital near Kondapur with INR 90-95 crore monthly revenue potential, and a Kakinada hospital currently at INR 7-8 crore a month, targeting INR 15-20 crore. O&M means no losses borne by KIMS.
Future pipeline: greenfield in Karnataka (300-350 beds, expandable by about 100) and acquisitions in Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Andhra; timing and bed count not committed.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala cost increase and steady-state margin, plus whether the Q1 ARPOB jump is structural or seasonal.
qa_highlights.answer: Kerala is in growth phase; single-digit EBITDA margin now, mid-teens next financial year, and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Management said ARPP is the better metric; ARPOB moves with seasonal case mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why Telangana occupancy sits around 50-52% and whether it can rise further.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bed count includes 250 demolished Secunderabad beds not yet operational; ex-Kondapur and ex-200 renovating beds occupancy is about 61%. 70% is achievable in three to four years without new beds.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost impact after the INR 1,100 crore debt repayment.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said QIP proceeds arrived around 24 June and debt was repaid on 27-28 June, so the interest saving was not in Q1 and will show from Q2. Debt was INR 2,570 crore at 30 June, about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments.

qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operative costs about INR 1.5-2 crore a month; Q1 losses marginal. Old hospital runs about six more months at about INR 90 lakh a month rent plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Thane ramp-up lagging peers and when it turns breakeven.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a four-to-five-month empanelment delay and seasonality. Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% margin; a healthy margin is expected if the trend holds.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana margin: why 30% guidance versus historical 35% peaks.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-35% over time, citing FY25-26 margins of about 31%, Secunderabad at 34-35% and Q4 FY26 Telangana at 38-39%. Return to 30%-plus will take time as new beds ramp.

Average revenue per operating bed +9.7% YoY and +0.1% QoQ; ARPP +6.8% YoY and -3.8% QoQ. Management said ARPP is the better indicator, as ARPOB moves with ALOS and seasonal case mix.

Kondapur commissioned with first patient on 20 June 2026; July (first full month) revenue about INR 45 crore versus INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Management said Kondapur full potential is about INR 100 crore per month within four to five years.

Bengaluru ARPOB running at INR 90,000+ for two quarters; management guided INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, with ARPP said to be similar to Telangana. Mahadevapura census-bed occupancy about 40%.

Insurance empanelment: about 50% of insurers done; remaining 50% covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets expected by end-August to mid-September 2026. Maharashtra Q1 hit by four-to-five-month empanelment delay; Thane July revenue INR 21 crore at about 10% EBITDA margin.
risks_watch: Empanelment: remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, due by end-August to mid-September 2026; the Joint Insurance Committee common-empanelment process is unresolved.

Acquisitions and greenfield timing not committed; management declined to quantify bed additions for FY28-29 and said the O&M deals (Golden Lan, Sarvottam) are draft-stage.
key_quotes: The first month has been very promising. We grew by almost 40% in less than a month.
As far as Telangana is concerned, we do not see any reason why we cannot ramp up to 70%, in spite of the new Kondapur hospital and the new Secunderabad hospital over the next three to four years.
I think it is too aggressive. Four to five is a good number.

Margins compressed on higher construction costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at ~10.85% in Q4 versus 17.5% a year earlier, which included a one-time claim of INR47.5 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of ~15% and new order wins of INR20,000-22,000 crore, while order book stands at ~INR26,470 crore.

Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

Competitive intensity was described as unchanged, with management choosing to keep marketing spend high to capture cheap new customers. Management declined to disclose store-level, geographic-split, warehouse-capacity and ad-mix data, and said it will keep reinvesting incremental food delivery margin into growth.

Management said competitive intensity in food delivery rose in Q2 and that Eternal is investing more in customer acquisition and frequency, with margins expected to stay broadly flat over the next 1-2 years. In quick commerce, management said the 12-month competitive spike is over, which gives it confidence to re-accelerate store expansion, mainly in smaller cities, starting October-December quarter. Management also discussed dark.ai, a privacy-focused AI application for power users, which is unmonetised and carried in the Others segment.

543325|2026-03.headline: Rolex Rings FY26 revenue held flat at INR1,144 crore despite a ~30% U.S. export drop; FY27 guided to 15-17% growth.
543325|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was about INR1,144 crore, broadly flat year on year, as a roughly 30% fall in U.S. exports was offset by Europe growth of about 25% and domestic growth of about 50%. Gross margin rose to 51.5% from 49.4%, attributed mainly to product mix, and operating EBITDA was held above 20%. Q4 other expenses were inflated by about INR22 crore of U.S. customs duty (about half recoverable from customers) and about INR6 crore of one-time legal and professional costs tied to the lender settlement. The company completed the INR101 crore Right of Recompense payment to lenders on March 31, 2026, and announced a INR180 crore buyback at INR180 per share, from which promoters are not participating.

543325|2026-06.headline: Rolex Rings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% to INR304 crore on labour-constrained output, while EBITDA margin expanded to 22.6% and PAT grew 22% to INR60 crore.
543325|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR304 crore, up 4.3% YoY, which management said was short of its guided growth because a shop-floor labour shortage in April to mid-June limited output, not demand. Auto components grew 13.5% to INR163 crore while bearing rings fell 6% to INR118 crore, with softness concentrated in domestic and European industrial bearing rings. EBITDA was INR69 crore at a 22.6% margin (up 100 bps YoY) and PAT rose 22% to INR60 crore, the third straight quarter of YoY margin expansion. Management said operations normalised from June, July 2026 was the highest-revenue month since inception, and it reiterated mid-teen FY27 revenue growth guidance while cutting its margin guidance to 21-22% citing ocean freight costs.

543330|2026-03.headline: Devyani Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.5% YoY to INR 1,437 crore, with KFC SSSG at 4.9%, its best in 14 quarters.
543330|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 18.5% YoY to INR 1,437 crore, and FY26 revenue crossed INR 5,500 crore at INR 5,611 crore. KFC returned to positive SSSG of 4.9% with nearly 15% YoY revenue growth, driven by a shift in focus to dine-in customers and store-level deals. Pizza Hut SSSG stayed negative at -3.7% and brand contribution was slightly negative, while the international business grew 20% YoY. Management is pursuing the Sapphire Foods merger, targeting completion by end of FY27, and is rebuilding the leadership team. Store count was 2,256 at year end, with negative net additions in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How do the leadership changes (CTO, CMO, COO) support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hired Neeraj Tiwari as CTO, Sandeep Anand as CMO (also overseeing Pizza Hut operations), and announced a COO from FMCG and technology backgrounds who joins in the next couple of weeks. Other appointments cover Costa and smaller brands. The aim is in-house technology capability and operational transformation.

qa_highlights.question: Are the store closures a deliberate clean-up, and does guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 negative store count reflects a reset in BD strategy toward better-quality stores and shutting loss-making units. FY27 guidance of 200 to 225 net additions, including 110 to 120 KFC, is unchanged.

qa_highlights.answer: Favourable raw and packing material costs, deal restructuring favouring dine-in, and a shift of promotions from online to offline. Menu price correction was below 0.5 percentage point.

qa_highlights.question: Split of KFC SSSG between AOV and transactions; Pizza Hut revival timing?

543330|2026-06.headline: Devyani Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore, with record Operating EBITDA of INR 151 crore (9.6% margin).
543330|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore and Operating EBITDA rose about 38% YoY to INR 151 crore, the company's highest ever, at a 9.6% margin. KFC returned to positive SSSG (3.3%) with dine-in salience improving to 57%, while Pizza Hut remained loss-making at brand contribution level with SSSG of -2.2%. Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a weak monsoon outlook and volatile macro, and said Sapphire merger approvals from NSE and BSE were received in June with completion targeted by end FY27.

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: SSSG +3.3%, revenue INR 684 crore (~+12% YoY), gross margin 69.4%, brand contribution INR 115 crore; offline saliency 57%, up over 3 pp YoY. Management targets 59-60% dine-in share and ADS of 105k-110k for 20%+ brand contribution margin.

segments.name: Pizza Hut
segments.commentary: SSSG -2.2% (improving sequentially), ADS up to ~INR 32,400 per store per day, revenue INR 184 crore, gross margin 76.3%, brand contribution loss INR 4 crore; 626 stores at quarter end.

segments.commentary: Biryani By Kilo SSSG +7.2%, Vaango +7.1%; combined revenue INR 98 crore, gross margin 65.9%, brand contribution ~INR 10 crore (10.2%). 218 stores including 23 BBK Express; BBK target INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years.

KFC marketing rebalanced from deep online discounting toward dine-in visits.

Franchise brands gross margin fell to 74.6% on higher input costs, offset by better cost management.

qa_highlights.question: What drivers beyond SSSG could lift KFC margins from ~17% and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the key lever is ADS; crossing 105k-110k ADS should take KFC brand contribution above 20%. Other levers are dine-in promotion, operating leverage and technology adoption, which will only deliver a few quarters after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC dine-in salience return to 60-65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65% is not achievable near term given convenience preference, especially in the North; the target is 59-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SSSG not guided higher after 13 quarters of negative trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited tough macro (rupee, oil, LPG availability) and said a bullish view needs a stable environment that it does not yet see.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Pizza Hut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3-way structure with Sapphire and Yum! held back decisions and innovation; product, ingredient and price-ladder work is underway, with full push after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate and leadership build-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters are supportive on investment; new COO, CTO and CMO have been hired, with joinings ranging from 2 weeks to 2 months; the whole leadership team is now in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Sapphire integration be straightforward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IT stacks and processes are largely similar because technology was run by Yum!, so integration should not be a major challenge.

qa_highlights.question: Why has KFC lagged some peers sequentially, and what is October trending like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed part of the gap to Navratri shifting into Q2 for peers, while Durga Puja (a KFC tailwind in south and east) shifted into Q3; expects Q2+Q3 to be similar to peers and targets Q3 SSSG slightly above Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is Pizza Hut moving to a value-focused, transaction-led strategy post-merger?

qa_highlights.question: Is inflation fully in the P&L or are there further headwinds?

qa_highlights.question: Will KFC gross margin fall further?

qa_highlights.question: What drove Biryani By Kilo's turnaround and can it reach 20%+ margin?

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC SSSG for Q2+Q3 be 8-9% as Sapphire indicated?

Adjusted PAT grew 25% to INR99 crore against INR79 crore a year earlier, though the prior-year reported PAT of INR160 crore included an INR81 crore deferred tax credit. 543333|2026-03.headline: CarTrade Q4 FY26 PAT rose 54% YoY to INR70.8 crore; FY26 PAT INR243 crore (+68%), with management targeting INR1,000 crore profit in 4-5 years.
543333|2026-03.overview: CarTrade reported a strong Q4 FY26 with consolidated EBITDA up 55% and margin at 35% for the quarter, and FY26 revenue up 22% with EBITDA margin at 33%. Consumer group (CarWale, BikeWale) grew revenue 25% in the quarter and 30% for the year. OLX India total income grew 16% in the quarter, below the ~18% of the prior quarter, which drew repeated analyst questions. Management pointed to new OLX monetisation products (Elite Buyer, Verification, Super Dost) as the next growth driver, but disclosed that these were still insignificant in revenue terms (under 5% of FY26 revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Why did OLX growth slow from about 18% to 15.5-16% QoQ despite guidance of stronger momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to two fewer days in the quarter, typical October-December seasonality, and Verification launching about 45 days later than planned. It said it was more optimistic than last quarter, with no change in outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What share of OLX revenue comes from Elite Buyer and Verification, and how big could it become in three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Elite Buyer and Verification were under 5% of FY26 revenue. Management said they will become significant in FY27 but gave no sizing; it said the revenue could be more than 30-40% over time, with no ceiling.

qa_highlights.question: How has the remarketing mix (repossession vs retail) and value-added fee share changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said institutional (repossession) volumes are not cyclical and both segments should keep growing. Inspection fees are under 10% of revenue; other fees are mostly auction-linked. Financing is a planned new fee line.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI or ChatGPT-style search threaten the traffic and consumer business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said traffic has grown as search has grown, that proprietary data, OEM/dealer integrations and brand give defensibility, and that AI is a net opportunity for the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROE about 10% and what is the plan for the cash of about INR1,244 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash balance is the main reason for the low ROE. Returning cash or M&A is possible in 2-3 years once tax shelters and loss carry-forwards allow; no specific M&A is in view.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan any acquisitions, such as the AutoMall stake?

543336|2026-03.headline: Chemplast Q4 FY26 net loss of INR45 crores on INR898 crore CCVL impairment; consolidated EBITDA rose to INR194 crores from INR37 crores.
543336|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR1,256 crores and EBITDA jumped to INR194 crores from INR37 crores, but the company posted a net loss of INR45 crores. The quarter absorbed an INR898 crore non-cash impairment on the investment in CCVL (suspension PVC) and a INR150 crore exceptional charge at CCVL for onerous contracts and raw material write-down. Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

qa_highlights.question: Are SPVC spreads still weak and could FY27 remain stressful for CCVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spreads are at neutral replacement cost, with VCM prices softening slightly. It acknowledged a couple more onerous contracts hit production in May-June and called FY27 a pessimistic-case risk, while Chinese producers are also under cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the impairment taken and what cash-flow outlook underpins it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impairment reflects the current view with no regulatory support. At today's prices, margins are only covering variable costs; the impairment would be reviewed periodically if conditions improve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR150 crore exceptional item and how will Q1 be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: It is the gap between actual cost and net realisable value at 31 March, expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. One or two more consignments could carry small contribution differences, and the business is roughly breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government likely to restore the 7.5% duty, and what other measures are in play?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry bodies are pushing for the duty to return at end-June. They are also seeking minimum import prices and QCO reinstatement; ADD is seen as the only long-term WTO-compliant solution.

qa_highlights.question: Has an ADD application on Chinese PVC been filed?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet. Data is being compiled and filing is expected in the near future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R32 export strategy and quota status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working with partners on export sales; domestic and export are both planned. It expects a quota allocation by 2027 and said the baseline survey runs to end-2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the custom manufacturing and LOI-backed revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify total LOI value. Six LOIs have been signed out of 17 commercial molecules, and the INR1,000 crore target is retained for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate of the independent director committee?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a broad review of portfolio reorganisation and M&A opportunities. Specialty capital allocation remains the priority, and no outcome has been predetermined.

rows.label: Order book toward INR 8,000-8,200 crore by decade end

543358|2026-06.headline: Sansera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR10,213 million, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and ADS order book lifted to about INR57.5 billion.
543358|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR10,213 million, up 33% YoY, with non-auto sales of INR1,998 million up 129.9% and 20.8% of sales. EBITDA excluding exceptionals was INR1,961 million (19.2% margin, up about 200 bps YoY), after a INR126 million provision for US import duty recovery. A INR169 million exceptional litigation settlement cut reported PAT to INR874 million (8.6% margin, up 39% YoY); PAT excluding the exceptional post-tax impact was about INR1,000 million. Management raised FY27 growth commentary to high-teens, with a possible 20% plus, and said the ADS order book rose to about INR57.5 billion after a post-quarter SEM order win.

financial_highlights.value: INR169 million pre-tax; INR127 million post-tax

segments.name: ADS (aerospace, defense, semicon)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,454 million, more than 3x YoY; primary non-auto growth driver. Management guides ADS growth of about 75-80% in FY27.

segments.name: Auto ICE
segments.commentary: INR6,275 million, +20.8% YoY on a high base; record quarter across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and scooters.

segments.name: Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV
segments.commentary: INR1,316 million, +22.2% YoY; record quarter, driven by EV adoption in two-wheelers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth now guided at high-teens, with management saying 20% or more is possible; non-ADS business expected to grow mid-teens to high-teens.
EBITDA margin: management wants to inch toward 19% (FY26 was 18.1%) and says Q1 may be elevated by mix, currency and about 40% international revenue; focus is on sustaining margin while growing.
ADS and export EBITDA margins targeted at 25-30%, with the upper end over time as utilisation rises.

ADS order book: about INR57.5 billion cumulative, executable over five years, versus INR44.4 billion at quarter end; the base business peak annual revenue is INR18.5 billion, to be achieved in about three years.
Management said ADS revenue will not reach INR1,500 crore next year; a FY28 revenue number will be guided toward end of FY27.

Long-term base plan: about INR3,500 crore revenue capacity by FY31 (INR5,700 crore confirmed ADS backlog executable by FY31); management reiterated INR8,000-9,000 crore total revenue opportunity by about FY31.
capex_capacity: Surface treatment facility next to ADS plant inaugurated; NADCAP validation in process, expected within about one to two months.
80,000 sq ft hangar for aero and SEM being built, commissioning expected in a month or two; customer line validation to follow.
Defense business relocating to a dedicated facility; sheet metal entry planned first via defense, later aerospace.
Build-to-suit facility of about 100,000 sq ft near the existing site under negotiation (targeted for August), ready in about 10 months.

Capacity targets: existing facility with extended hangar supports INR1,400-1,500 crore revenue; defense about INR500 crore over five years; new facility about INR1,500 crore; total about INR3,500 crore by FY31.

Auto capex: crankshaft and connecting rod forging/machining at Pantnagar (Plant 6) and Manesar (Plant 4); machining at Bangalore Plant 2 for xEV; new multi-storey building at Plant 2; projects to commission from start of Q3 FY27, completion within about a year.
ADS asset turns of 2.0-2.25x cited. Management has not updated the FY27 capex quantum given last quarter; capex phased to customer validation and utilisation.
demand_pricing: Domestic two-wheeler and passenger vehicle demand strong; management sees visibility for about one and a half quarters, with festive-season demand into Q3.
Supply chain stress on raw material and child parts; customers helping secure material.

Material cost inflation mainly in aluminium and consumables; steel inflation limited. Pass-through of steel inflation and higher tool and labour costs (mainly northern plants) still under negotiation, with nothing booked in Q1.
Forex movement gave a short-term cushion to realisations.

Exports: traction in passenger vehicles, premium two-wheelers and off-road; deliveries to a North American energy customer to give sustained revenue from Q3. Customers sourcing more from India as a stopgap while the US connecting-rod plant awaits tariff clarity.
Order wins in the quarter: about INR88 crore in PV/CV and INR75 crore in two-wheelers (normal course, per management).
Management said Sansera's motorcycle revenue grew about 12.5% and it is gaining share at TVS, Yamaha and Suzuki; it supplies about 75% of Maruti's volumes for the components it makes.

SEM order (post-quarter, after 1 July cutoff): about $75 million annual business from an existing customer; about INR5,700 crore, roughly INR1,250 crore over five years. Revenue starts calendar 2027 and peaks in calendar 2029, gated by mother-machine lead times.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ADS order book about INR45 bn or INR57 bn, are incremental orders from existing or new customers, and where does ADS revenue go in 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR44.4 bn book at quarter end rose to about INR57.5 bn after a post-1 July SEM order from an existing customer, about $75 mn annual business, about INR5,700 crore executable over five years (to FY31). Revenue ramp is gated by mother-machine lead times, with significant revenue from calendar 2027 and peak in calendar 2029.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR129 million impact included in the 19.2% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vikas Goel confirmed the US import duty provision is included in EBITDA, treated as a cost.

qa_highlights.question: ADS asset turns and capex implications for semicon and aerospace capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Hari Krishnan put ADS asset turns at about 2.0-2.25x on peak revenue versus assets. Capacity: 80,000 sq ft hangar commissioning in a month or two, a build-to-suit ~100,000 sq ft facility under negotiation (targeted August) and ready in about 10 months, all within about 500 metres.

qa_highlights.question: Can non-ADS grow mid-teens and total top-line reach high-teens to 20%+ in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said non-ADS should grow mid-teens easily, moving toward mid-to-high teens as momentum allows, and overall growth of high-teens to 20% is a good possibility if trends sustain. He noted 2-3 year visibility of 20%+ is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How did material costs and pricing pass-through play out, and was the gross margin expansion from mix alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Goel said material inflation was modest, mainly aluminium and some consumables, with limited steel inflation. Steel and tool/labour pass-through is under negotiation with nothing booked in Q1. Mix and forex both supported gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ICE crankshaft and connecting rod capacities expanding, and what is the updated capex number?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham linked the expansion to two-wheeler OEMs outsourcing crankshafts, plus PV indications. Rahul Kale described a fully automated Pantnagar crankshaft facility, forging, heat treatment and Bangalore conrod machining. Vikas Goel said the FY27 capex plan given last quarter has not been updated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%-plus growth through FY29 prudent, and does ADS margin reach 20-25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said it is too early to call 20%+ for two to three years, since auto expansions take 18-24 months and need two-year customer visibility. On margins, he said Q1 may be elevated by mix and currency, exports and ADS target 25-30% EBITDA, and FY26 margin was 18.1%.

risks_watch: Supply chain stress on raw material and child parts, with customers helping to secure material; could constrain volumes in the festive quarters.
Mother-machine lead times (7-9 months, sometimes up to 9) and validation/NADCAP timing could delay ADS ramp; NADCAP for surface treatment expected in 1-2 months.
Pass-through of steel, tool and labour inflation (mainly northern plants) not booked in Q1; Q1 margin may be elevated by mix and forex.
US connecting-rod plant still awaiting tariff clarity; US import duty recovery of INR126 million unresolved and provided on recovery-risk basis.
Capex quantum not updated since last quarter; new facility and build-to-suit timelines (August negotiation, ~10 months) and 18-24 month auto expansion lead times.
Semicon demand concentration tied to AI-driven boom; aerospace risk seen as lower, tied to Boeing and Airbus programs.
Management raised FY27 growth guidance to high-teens with 20%+ possible; FY28 revenue guidance to come toward end FY27.
Motorcycle wallet-share question unresolved: management cited about 12.5% motorcycle revenue growth versus industry volume growth of 17-18%; to be checked offline.
key_quotes: We started FY2 7 on a very strong note, delivering our highest -ever quarterly revenue while maintaining healthy profitability.
So right now it is INR5,700 crores executable by FY 2031.
Not to say that is a number we target to really reach. Orders are being negotiated. Conversions are at an advanced stage.
The exact numbers we will be able to give you a guidance towards the end of this year, depending upon the status of our plan, the status of validation, so many other factors.
543358|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on ADS order momentum and domestic two-wheeler and PV demand, but cautious on quantifying FY28 ADS revenue, margins beyond FY27 and the capex update, with several answers deferred to end-FY27 guidance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 19.2% in Q1 (up ~200 bps from 17.2%) vs FY26 18.1%, management wants to inch toward 19%, and ADS/export margins are targeted at 25-30%; but Q1 is flattered by mix and forex and steel/labour pass-through of nothing booked yet.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed (no number given), FY27 capex quantum has not been updated since last quarter, and build-to-suit facility is under negotiation for August, so a formal capex update is plausible but tied to customer validation and end-FY27 guidance.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth already raised to high-teens with 20%+ described as a good possibility, and Q1 grew 33% YoY, but management declined to call 20%+ visibility beyond FY27.

rows.when: revenue ramp from calendar 2027, peak calendar 2029

543363|2026-03.headline: Prevest DenPro FY26 revenue rose 13.9% to INR71.81 crore and PAT rose 12.9% to INR20.49 crore, with PAT margin at 26.7%.
543363|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 13.9% to INR71.81 crore, with exports up 17.58% and domestic up 9%. EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR29.62 crore, though the EBITDA margin of 38.6% moderated slightly year on year. Q4 FY26 revenue grew only 2.63% to INR18.94 crore due to geopolitical disruption and shipping issues, but Q4 profitability outpaced sales, with EBITDA margin at 40.87% and PAT up 13.23% to INR5.82 crore. Management launched disinfectant commercialisation and set up a UAE subsidiary, whose operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 domestic sales grew 9%; H2 domestic sales rose 12.72% YoY and 16.19% HoH. Management cited floods and GST changes as H1 drags.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export sales grew 17.58%; H2 exports rose 11.66% YoY and 3.56% HoH. The company says it covers about 90-92 countries.

segments.name: US (Axiodent and private label)
segments.commentary: US business grew about 37.58% (also cited as 38%) in FY26, driven by online sales, direct orders and private-label business won at US exhibitions.

segments.name: Oradox oral care
segments.commentary: Sales declined about 2% in FY26 because US MoCRA-related exports and a planned Dubai consignment did not ship. Management expects 2-3 new launches and a recovery.

segments.name: 3D printing (resins and printers)
segments.commentary: 3D resin revenue rose about 40.5% YoY. 3D printers (brand Omni, sales started November 2025) rose about 162% from a low base.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Oradox to compensate for the FY26 shortfall this year, supported by 2-3 new product launches.
UAE subsidiary expected to start online sales in Dubai the following month, after product registration; commercial operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.
Company aims for a fully indigenous 3D printer by 2028.
Management expects at least 40% of dental-office procedures to have a digital workflow within five years.
Management is cautious on global uncertainty but sees the domestic market, Tier 2/3 expansion and disinfectants as growth drivers.
capex_capacity: Traditional capacity utilisation is about 67-68% of installed capacity; at full installed capacity, turnover would be about INR125 crore (Vinay Jamwal).
New production lines (digital dentistry, resins, disinfectants, oral health) are running at about 18-20% utilisation and are expected to rise.
Four R&D test licences for new agents (caries removal, endodontic irrigants, self-etching resins, periodontal gels) are at TRL 7, with two products launched in the market in the month of the call.
Import substitution of raw materials is in progress through in-house development.
Subsidiaries in the UAE (opened February 2026) and the US (Axiodent) are operating; two sales staff employed in Dubai.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian manufacturing cost advantage and high import duties make it hard for MNCs to beat the company on price; it also cites quality certifications.
The company is an OEM supplier to about 3-4 large companies and expects to add a couple more in the next two years.
Competitors named for digital dentistry include Ivoclar, Dentsply and 3Shape; management says digital dentistry is a level playing field, unlike legacy products where MNCs have first-mover advantage.
Disinfectants launched this year, with an early customer response described as highly encouraging; no revenue figure given.
Oradox was hit by US MoCRA cosmetic-regulation requirements and by the Middle East conflict, which blocked a planned Dubai consignment.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth slowed over the last 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 export growth of 17.5% is satisfactory given geopolitical headwinds, and that the company is shifting share from disrupted Asian markets to other geographies across 90-92 countries.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is spent on R&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sai Kalyan did not give a figure and said it would be provided later. He described two products launched, four licences at TRL 7 and import substitution work.

qa_highlights.question: What do the UAE and US subsidiaries do, and how is Dubai responding?
qa_highlights.answer: The US subsidiary, Axiodent, drove US growth of about 37.58% through online sales, direct orders and private labelling. The Dubai subsidiary opened in February 2026, hired two sales staff and is registering products for online sales expected next month.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Jamwal said traditional capacity runs at 67-68% utilisation, which would imply about INR125 crore turnover at full installed capacity. New lines run at 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove domestic performance and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaibhav Munjal cited expansion of Tier 2/3 distribution, a larger in-house sales team and new products such as disinfectants and Rotoflex. H1 was hit by floods and GST changes, and H2 recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How is Oradox trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said sales fell about 2% because US and Dubai exports were blocked by MoCRA rules and the war. Management expects recovery through marketing, direct-to-doctor programmes and 2-3 launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3D printing opportunity and right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said digital dentistry is a level field where the company has a slight edge, with 3D resin revenue up about 40.5% and printer sales up about 162%, and an indigenous printer targeted for 2028.

risks_watch: Q4 revenue growth of only 2.63% was hit by war-related shipping disruption and customer order delays; the trend in Q1 FY27 needs monitoring.
Capacity utilisation is 67-68% for traditional lines and only 18-20% for new lines, so new-line ramp-up is unproven.
Dubai subsidiary has not yet started commercial operations and depends on the Middle East situation.
Oradox is declining and needs the planned launches and US/Dubai registrations to recover.
The R&D spend figure was not provided and the disinfectant revenue contribution is undisclosed.
Management said the Chairman was ill, and the June 2 call was cancelled; continuity of leadership needs watching.

543364|2026-03.headline: Markolines reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore (up from Rs 307 crore) and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore (about 15% higher), with EPS up 17% to Rs 11.90.
543364|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore against Rs 307 crore a year earlier, EBITDA of Rs 48.54 crore and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore, with EPS rising from Rs 10.16 to Rs 11.90. Q4 revenue was about Rs 105 crore with a stated PAT margin of about 10.81% and EBITDA margin of about 18%. Management said West Asia-related disruption weighed on performance during the year. The call centred on the pending merger with Markolines Infra, a targeted FY27 growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, and an active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore. Several answers on margins, order book and merger timing were qualitative or repeated.

segments.name: Highway maintenance (pavement)
segments.commentary: About 65% of revenue as of March 2026, per management; Rs 350 crore pavement revenue cited for FY26. Covers preventive, major (5 to 7 year cycle) and rigid pavement maintenance.

segments.name: Specialized construction
segments.commentary: About 35% of revenue as of March 2026, up from about 25% per analyst question; includes micro-surfacing, cold in-place recycling (CIPR), soil stabilisation, FDR, tunnelling and bridges. Management says it carries higher margins.

segments.name: Markolines Infra (proposed merger)
segments.commentary: Cited at about Rs 150 crore FY26 revenue; operates about 60 work orders across about 30 projects including 28 toll projects. Management said its PAT margin is 9 to 10%, above pavement, and monthly billing is about Rs 14 to 15 crore.

segments.name: School and sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Newly entered; one open school infrastructure order and two smaller sports complex rehabilitation orders in Andhra Pradesh. No value disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, per management; Markolines Infra revenue would be additional on merger.
Merger with Markolines Infra expected to be completed by end of FY27; management cites about six months for NCLT processes, with all queries answered and none pending.
Target closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore by end of FY27.
Target of Rs 1,000 crore revenue scale in about three years, with possibility to bring it forward.
Capex of about Rs 10 crore in FY27 for one or more pavers and possibly one HMP; policy of not exceeding Rs 10 crore per year.
Management expects monsoon at about 90% of average this year; first two quarters to see lower revenue.
capex_capacity: No major capex in FY26, per management.
Plan for one or a few additional pavers and possibly one HMP, about Rs 10 crore in FY27.
Company owns three sets of machinery; other machinery is rented locally where cheaper.
Plants and equipment are churned about every 3 to 4 years to maintain efficiency.
Eligible to bid up to Rs 500 crore projects on its own following completion of a Maharashtra tunnel project.
demand_pricing: Order book about Rs 600 crore plus, split roughly 45-50% maintenance and 50-55% specialized construction (management gave both 50-50 and 45-45 figures). Infra order book is separate and recurring.
Active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore across four to five projects of Rs 300 to 500 crore each; management says it wins at least 50% of targeted orders.
L1 position on a Rs 120 crore maintenance contract with a corporation, per management.
Management says it works on a cost-plus basis with clients, so PBT and PAT margins are steady (7 to 8%), while EBITDA varies with client capex pass-through.
Management says maintenance is about 15% of road cost in India versus about 40% globally, which it sees as a long-term driver.
Government allowed sovereign and international funds to participate in PPP highway construction, which management sees as increasing demand for O&M partners.

qa_highlights.question: Status of merger with Markolines Infra and expected completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Applications filed and all queries answered in March, with few recently answered; management expects about six months to completion and a merged entity by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margins of Infra and combined FY27 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Infra results to be released within a week after final audit; Infra margins are higher than pavement, with PAT of about 9 to 10% for services. Management later said PBT and PAT margins stay at 7 to 8%.

qa_highlights.question: FY26 and FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex in FY26; about Rs 10 crore planned in FY27 for pavers and possibly one HMP, with equipment churned every 3 to 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Win ratio and closing order book expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Win ratio of at least 50% on targeted active orders; management targets a closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore, versus an 18-month typical coverage norm.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth of at least 30% standalone, driven by higher eligibility after the tunnel project; margin guidance was not given, as EBITDA is said to vary with client capex pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall in Q4, and what drove the 62% QoQ PAT jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses and material consumption must be viewed together because outsourcing shifts costs between heads, and margins should be similar. Q4 is seasonally strongest as billing concentrates in March.

risks_watch: Merger timing relies on NCLT approval; management expects completion within about six months.
Q4 seasonality: first two quarters are weaker due to monsoon, and management expects below-average rainfall this year.
Order book conversion: management's 50% win-rate claim and Rs 1,000 crore closing order book target are unverified.
Specialized construction share rising (about 35%), with the 50% of order book in multi-year contracts, which affects visibility and execution timing.
Margin variability: EBITDA is described as variable with client capex pass-through; PAT margin guidance is only 7 to 8%.
West Asia crisis cited as a drag on FY26 performance; no detail given on impact.

543384|2026-06.headline: Nykaa Q1 FY27: net revenue up 29% YoY to INR 2,782 crore, EBITDA up 68% to INR 236 crore at 8.5% margin, PAT INR 80 crore.
543384|2026-06.overview: Nykaa reported GMV of INR 5,590 crore (+34% YoY) and net revenue of INR 2,782 crore (+29% YoY) for Q1 FY27, with gross margin up 123 bps to 45.9%. EBITDA rose 68% to INR 236 crore (8.5% margin, up about 196 bps YoY) and PAT reached INR 80 crore (2.9% margin). Beauty NSV grew 29% with a 10.3% EBITDA margin, while Fashion NSV grew 54% and turned breakeven at the EBITDA level (0.1% margin) with the business profitable overall. Management also announced the acquisition of a 51% stake in dermocosmetic brand Aminu, with the balance to follow over several years.
